articles.title: Chiefs Rookie Emmett Johnson Scores a Touchdown in His First NFL Start Against Atlanta; How an Unexpected Opportunity Became an Early Career Milestone
articles.summary: Emmett Johnson made the most of his big break when the Kansas City Chiefs gave him his first NFL start against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body: Emmett Johnson made the most of his big break when the Kansas City Chiefs gave him his first NFL start against the Atlanta Falcons. After an injury opened up a spot, he stepped up and played a great game. He proved he can both run the ball and catch passes, which gave the Chiefs another dependable playmaker. Scoring two touchdowns was a huge early milestone in his pro career, and it quickly won him praise from his teammates and coaches.Emmett Johnson's Journey to the Kansas City ChiefsJohnson earned his reputation as a star back during his time at Nebraska. In 2025, he put together a huge season with 1,451 rushing yards and 12 scores, which earned him Big Ten Running Back of the Year honors and a spot on the AP All-American second team. His strong play caught the eye of NFL scouts. The Kansas City Chiefs selected him in the fifth round with the 161st overall pick in April 2026.The Opportunity That Put Him in the Starting LineupJohnson spent the start of the season waiting his turn behind established starter Kenneth Walker III. When a groin injury kept Walker out of the Week 10 game against Atlanta on November 15, 2026, Johnson finally got his shot. The Chiefs turned to their rookie, giving him his first NFL start. Although the opportunity came at short notice, Johnson had already been learning the team's offensive system and preparing for a larger role.Emmett Johnson's Breakthrough Against AtlantaJohnson wasted little time making an impact at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. During Kansas City's opening scoring drive, he caught a 12-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter. He later added another touchdown reception, this time on a six-yard pass in the fourth quarter. Both scores came through the air, showing that Johnson could offer more than just a running option in the Chiefs' offense.Johnson finished the game with 101 rushing yards on 22 carries and six receptions for 70 yards. His 171 total yards from scrimmage and two receiving touchdowns made him one of Kansas City's standout performers in the 35-13 victory. He also recorded 10 forced missed tackles, according to NFL Pro data cited by Sports Illustrated.Johnson's Early NFL Career MilestoneThe Atlanta game was a big step forward for Johnson because it showed how quickly he was picking up the pro game. Head coach Andy Reid praised how well-prepared the rookie was, especially for knowing the playbook, doing his blocking jobs well, and protecting the quarterback. Reid also mentioned that Johnson has clearly earned the trust of his teammates. Those qualities helped him handle the responsibility of starting when the Chiefs needed him.Johnson's performance also caught the attention of Mahomes, who praised his ability to run hard, break tackles, and make plays as a receiver. The quarterback was pleased to see the rookie take advantage of an opportunity that had arrived with little notice.What Lies Ahead for Emmett Johnson? His Potential Role in the Chiefs' OffenseJohnson’s strong game against Atlanta gave Kansas City another weapon in its running back rotation. Even though the Chiefs expected Kenneth Walker III back for their next game against the Arizona Cardinals, having both backs ready gives Andy Reid’s offense a nice boost, especially with Johnson's pass-catching skills and depth.For Johnson, the challenge will be to maintain the same preparation and consistency as the season progresses. His first start showed that he could handle a bigger workload, but he will need to keep earning opportunities through his outstanding performances. The Atlanta game gave the rookie a strong foundation to build on as he continues his NFL journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Allen vs. Patrick Mahomes: Why Thanksgiving night in Buffalo is the NFL season's biggest quarterback showdown
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes meet Thursday night in Buffalo, and the numbers between them point in two directions.
articles.body: Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes meet Thursday night in Buffalo, and the numbers between them point in two directions. Allen is 5-1 against Mahomes in the regular season. Mahomes is 4-0 against Allen in the playoffs. Kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, and it will be the first Thanksgiving game the Bills have ever hosted. Buffalo leads the AFC and Kansas City arrives off three straight blowouts. Ten meetings since 2020 have produced an even split. Neither side wants to hand the other a win on a stage this big.Why Thanksgiving night in Buffalo is the season's biggest quarterback showdownNo other quarterback matchup this season carries this much weight. The Chiefs and Bills have played ten times since 2020, and each side has five wins. That sounds tidy. It is not. Allen has won five of the six regular season meetings. Mahomes has won all four in the playoffs.NBC has branded it the rivalry of the decade, and for once the billing does not feel like marketing. The game closes a Thanksgiving tripleheader that begins with Bears at Lions and Eagles at Cowboys. The broadcast starts at 7 p.m. ET on NBC, with streaming on Peacock.Allen's most recent win over Kansas City was a statement. He threw for 273 yards and accounted for three touchdowns, and Buffalo's defense kept Mahomes under pressure before stopping a late Kansas City drive that could have tied it.Mahomes has the other side of it. His last playoff win over Allen came in the 2025 AFC Championship Game, and he has never lost to him in the postseason.Pressure is the detail to watch. Buffalo bothered Mahomes in their last meeting. If it happens again, Kansas City will need Reid to find answers quickly.Then there is the holiday itself. Allen is 3-0 on Thanksgiving, with wins over Dallas, New Orleans and Detroit. None of those teams had Mahomes. Buffalo is 6-4-1 on the day overall but has never hosted one before. Travis Kelce already has a read on it. "Obviously, Pat Mahomes and Josh Allen is always an instant classic," the Chiefs tight end said.How the Chiefs and Bills arriveLast season hurt both teams, just in different ways. Kansas City went 6-11 and missed the playoffs, a rare miss for a franchise that had become a January regular. Buffalo went 12-5 and lost a heartbreaker to Denver in the divisional round.The Chiefs have found a rhythm. They led Arizona 34-7 in the fourth quarter Sunday, and Andy Reid sent Justin Fields in for Mahomes rather than risk an injury in a game that was over. It was their third blowout in a row.The prep window is short. Sunday's game left Kansas City with four days to get ready for Allen.Kansas City still has Travis Kelce and Xavier Worthy as targets for Mahomes. Buffalo has running back James Cook and receiver Khalil Shakir around Allen. Both offenses have options. Whoever's quarterback gets more time will probably decide it.Early lines made the Bills a three-point favorite, so Kansas City is the underdog on the road.Thursday is a regular season game, and that column has leaned Allen's way five to one. If Mahomes wants to change the pattern, Buffalo gives him a national stage to do it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “The best thing that we can do for our kids..:” How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $10,000 donation helped young children handle difficult emotions
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany Mahomes have continued to support children through their charitable work.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany Mahomes have continued to support children through their charitable work. In October 2024, the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation provided a $10,000 grant to KC Healthy Kids, helping the organisation create six Safe Spaces at two early learning centres in Shawnee, Kansas.The spaces give young children a place to manage difficult emotions, while teachers also receive training to better understand the behaviour of students dealing with challenges at home. The initiative focuses on helping children develop emotional skills from an early age.How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' foundation helped children find a safe spaceThe six Safe Spaces, also known as Calming Corners, offer children a quiet place inside their classrooms. Each area includes books, emotion charts, fidget toys, plush cushions and a tent with twinkling lights. These items help children understand their feelings and find ways to calm themselves.Shelby Nace, a bilingual social worker at KC Healthy Kids, explained the thinking behind the initiative in an interview with KSHB on October 16, 2024. “A lot of school districts across the country are kind of moving in this direction,” she said, before adding, “The strategy itself is rooted in mindfulness.”Nace also explained why children should learn these skills early. “The best thing that we can do for our kids is build in the resilience, and so that comes from the person to person connection, but that also comes from them having internal tools to regulate themselves,” she told KSHB.She further stressed, “The sooner the kids can be introduced to these strategies, the easier it will stick with them throughout their lives.”The programme also focuses on helping teachers recognise when a child's behaviour may reflect difficulties outside the classroom. Teachers received trauma-informed training to identify changes in students and respond with greater understanding. Instead of asking, “What is wrong with you?”, the approach encourages adults to ask, “What happened to you?”Preschool teacher Amy Powers, who works at New City Early Learning Academy, also shared her reaction to the initiative. “As an adult, I really wish something like this was around for me,” she told KSHB. She added, “It's working.”Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes continue their work to support childrenPatrick Mahomes established the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019 to improve children's lives through initiatives focused on health, wellness and underserved communities. Its work includes programmes that support education, youth development and access to opportunities.In October 2023, the foundation announced a $1.625 million contribution and a multi-year partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America. The commitment supports communities connected to Patrick and Brittany, including Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse.Patrick explained why the partnership was important to him. “We are truly excited to partner with Boys & Girls Clubs of America by investing in the future of children,” he said in the announcement. He also pointed to Brittany's own experience with the organisation, saying children who attend its clubs receive “the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose.”Brittany also spoke about what the partnership meant to them. “This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me,” she said. “We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”The Boys & Girls Clubs of America partnership also included a commitment from the foundation to donate $1,500 for every touchdown Patrick scores during the regular season. The Safe Spaces grant reflects another part of the foundation's work, supporting children by giving them resources to build confidence, develop healthy habits and handle challenges.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week 12 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Justice Hill, Konata Mumpfield, Cam Ward
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers, give yourselves a quick pat on the back.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers, give yourselves a quick pat on the back.

You all earned it after getting through the busiest bye week of the 2026 NFL season.

Since the schedule keeps moving, though, we already have to say goodbye to Bye-mageddon and turn attention to the unique challenge of Week 12, which will feature games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday and Monday. Things are about to get chaotic, so let's get ahead of the chaos with early waiver-wire targets to prioritize using roster percentages courtesy of FantasyPros .

Justice Hill, RB, Baltimore Ravens (26% Rostered)

Impact running backs can be hard to find this late in the season, but maybe Justice Hill can be an exception.

Now, that's probably overstating his potential, but there are reasons to at least believe the arrow is pointing up for him.

For starters, he looked pretty great in Week 11. He rushed for 69 yards and a touchdown (nearly two scores, but he fumbled through the end zone) while catching 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards. Plus, Ravens starter Derrick Henry was evaluated for a concussion late in that contest, so they might want to be cautious with their 32-year-old running back, since their season is going nowhere (six straight losses).

Hill's ceiling will be capped a bit as long as Henry is around, but Hill intrigues as a PPR flex play with 16 receptions on 23 targets over the last three weeks. And considering the juice he has shown in the running game (69-plus yards on single-digit carries two of his last three outings), he is arguing pretty loudly for an expanded role.

Konata Mumpfield, WR, Los Angeles Rams (19% Rostered)

Puka Nacua is done for the season following knee surgery, and Davante Adams doesn't sound particularly close to returning from his hamstring injury. It's possible, then, that this passing game might run through Konata Mumpfield.

And it could be an active aerial attack with the Rams squaring off in a potential shootout with the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night.

Before the Rams went on their Week 11 bye, Mumpfield effectively had a trial run as the team's top target against the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams didn't need to lean too heavily on their passing game then, but when they did, they looked Mumpfield's way more than any other receiver, and he gave them reasons to keep coming back by turning his four targets into three receptions for 81 yards and a touchdown.

It isn't often that Matthew Stafford's top target will be available on the waiver wire. Take advantage while you can.

Cam Ward, QB, Tennessee Titans (44% Rostered)

With the Titans more or less perpetually playing from behind, Cam Ward has a real chance to put up numbers.

And he's finally taking advantage of that.

Last year's top overall pick has thrown for more than 230 yards and multiple touchdowns in three consecutive contests. He's even rushed for 83 yards and a score over that stretch.

This is the kind of volume managers should be chasing on waivers, and it looks like it should last through this week, at least. Ward will tussle for the second time in three weeks against the Jaguars, and in the first meeting, he paired 231 passing yards and two touchdowns with 39 rushing yards.

articles.title: DK Metcalf Denies Trying to Poke Cooper DeJean in Eye, Addresses Altercation in Steelers-Eagles
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf remained somewhat mum on the circumstances that led to his ejection in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf remained somewhat mum on the circumstances that led to his ejection in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Metcalf said he "can't remember" the exact specifics of what transpired between him and Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean. He also suggested reporters should speak with DeJean to understand what provoked him on the field.

The two-time Pro Bowler did at least deny poking DeJean in the eye.

Metcalf received a second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in the third quarter against Philadelphia. That earned him an early exit.

Replays appeared to show him with his hand inside DeJean's facemask to draw the flag:

The ejection capped off a forgettable day for Metcalf, who caught one pass for two yards on four targets. He drew further scorn for leaving the stadium altogether immediately as the game ended.

The veteran wideout could face a possible suspension from the NFL if the league deems him to be a repeat offender. He has been ejected three times across his career, and he received a two-game ban last year after a confrontation with a fan.

Since his trade to the Steelers, Metcalf has 95 receptions for 1,284 yards and eight touchdowns in 25 games. That's not the kind of production you want from a receiver who's making $33 million annually.

And beyond the headaches he's giving Pittsburgh, one coach was sharply critical of Metcalf's effort level.

"He has 74 targets and three catching-radius wins," the coach told Mike Sando of The Athletic. "He is poor versus press. I'm talking, stand up, no moves, slow release, get jammed and give up on routes. Then he lacks the route speed to create separation. ... The catching radius part is unbelievable to me where they just don't do that. What else are you going to do with a guy who is not fast enough to separate, lets guys play into his body downfield and doesn't win?"

Metcalf is tied to the Steelers through the 2029 season. Right now, you'd bet he won't see out the remainder of his contract in the Steel City.

articles.title: Tom Brady sends blunt message to Hall of Fame voters as Bill Belichick gets another chance at Canton
articles.summary: Tom Brady has made it clear that he believes Bill Belichick belongs in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
articles.body: Tom Brady has made it clear that he believes Bill Belichick belongs in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. The former New England Patriots quarterback has once again spoken in support of his longtime coach, saying voters need to “come to their senses” after Belichick missed out on induction last year. With Belichick now advancing in the Class of 2027 selection process alongside Patriots owner Robert Kraft, Brady is hoping both men finally receive the recognition they deserve.Tom Brady defends Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft after Hall of Fame snubBrady shared his thoughts during Fox’s pregame show on Sunday, November 22, after Belichick and Kraft were announced as candidates for the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class. The seven-time Super Bowl champion congratulated everyone who had reached this stage but made it clear that seeing his former coach and team owner move forward was particularly special.“You know what? Congrats to everybody,” Brady said. “What an honor for all those guys, and I’m glad all the voters seem like they need to come to their senses on this one. These guys were just architects of what a two-decade dynasty was all about.”He also praised Kraft for everything he has done for the NFL before turning his attention to Belichick, with whom he shared some of the biggest moments of his career.“[Kraft], what he’s done for this league has just been exceptional. Bill [Belichick], c’mon, there’s nobody that I’d rather play for than him. I’m expecting August in Canton to be a big Patriot party,” Brady added.Brady’s words carry particular weight because he spent 20 seasons playing under Belichick in New England. Together, they won six Super Bowl championships and helped build one of the most successful teams in NFL history. Their partnership played a major role in making the Patriots a regular title contender for nearly two decades.Tom Brady previously called Bill Belichick his greatest coaching influenceThis is not the first time Brady has publicly stood up for Belichick’s Hall of Fame case. When the former Patriots coach failed to get inducted in his first year of eligibility, Brady strongly disagreed with the decision and sent a statement to Hall of Fame voters.“I don’t believe that any coach in the history of the game has done more to earn his place in the Hall of Fame than Bill Belichick,” Brady said.He also explained why Belichick had such a big influence on his career, pointing to the coach’s leadership, vision and daily discipline. Brady said those qualities helped the Patriots remain competitive at the highest level for almost 20 years.For Belichick, the latest development gives him another opportunity to reach Canton after last year’s disappointment. He won six Super Bowls as New England’s head coach and finished his NFL head coaching career with 333 wins, including playoff games, the second-highest total in league history.Kraft has also moved forward in the selection process in the contributor category, while Belichick represents the coaching category. Both will be considered alongside 13 modern-era player candidates. The selection committee will narrow the group before deciding who receives the required 80% support for induction.The Pro Football Hall of Fame will announce its Class of 2027 at NFL Honors in February, with the induction ceremony scheduled for August in Canton, Ohio. Brady could have another reason to celebrate if his former teammate Rob Gronkowski also makes the class. The modern-era player candidates are expected to be announced in January.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patriots HC Vrabel Addresses Daniel Jones, Jimmy Garoppolo Rumors After Drake Maye's Injury
articles.summary: The New England Patriots are sticking with Tommy DeVito while Drake Maye remains sidelined.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are sticking with Tommy DeVito while Drake Maye remains sidelined.

The team's head coach, Mike Vrabel, was asked by reporters if the team would consider adding the recently-released Daniel Jones and responded, "Tommy's our starter."

That comes after Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported last week that there has been "no serious discussion" within the Patriots organization of a Jimmy Garoppolo reunion.

The hope remains, however, that Maye eventually returns this season:

DeVito, 28, came on in relief of Maye during the team's Munich game against the Detroit Lions on Nov. 15, finishing 12-of-24 for 81 yards with a touchdown, an interception and four sacks taken. The Patriots lost, 35-10.

In 15 career games, DeVito has thrown for 1,490 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions. He's 3-5 in his eight starts.

Jones, 29, was released by the Indianapolis Colts following Thursday's 26-3 loss against the Houston Texans. He has an NFL-worst 13 interceptions on the season and the Colts are just 3-8 on the season.

Still, he would be a far more experienced option for New England than DeVito. And according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, "the Baltimore Ravens, Patriots and Arizona Cardinals are among the teams expected to at least consider signing Jones."

However, per that report, Jones is "unlikely to sign immediately, preferring to wait for the right opportunity with the right team at the right time."

New England, meanwhile, doesn't have total clarity on whether Maye will be able to return this season after fracturing his right fibula . While he won't require surgery and didn't suffer ligament damage, leaving open the the possibility, however slim, that he might return this season.

But in the meantime, it's DeVito time for the 5-5 Patriots.

articles.title: Abdul Carter Reveals If He 'Had a Tell on' Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars' 'Cadence' After Giants' Win
articles.summary: Your eyes may not have deceived you while watching New York Giants edge-rusher Abdul Carter wreak havoc on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.
articles.body:
Your eyes may not have deceived you while watching New York Giants edge-rusher Abdul Carter wreak havoc on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

The MMQB's Albert Breer asked Carter directly whether "must've had a tell on the Jaguars' cadence" based on a remark made during the CBS broadcast. The second-year defender didn't explicitly say as much, but he intuitively understood when to attack the pocket.

"Yeah, that was honestly just instinct," he said. "It's me trusting my get-off. And yeah, it paid off."

Carter called his shot. He teased a big performance on social media and delivered to the tune of two sacks, two tackles for loss and five hits on Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence.

Lawrence threw for 301 yards but was clearly affected by New York's consistent pass rush. He completed just 25 of his 47 attempts and had two interceptions.

Carter was underwhelming as a rookie. Considered one of the most pro-ready prospects in the 2025 draft, he finished with just four sacks and didn't become a regular starter until Week 12.

While the raw numbers aren't there — he doubled his season sack total Sunday —Carter is turning a corner, and the Jags game provided a proof of concept. Things might be starting to click for the former Penn State standout.

The 3-8 Indianapolis Colts are next on the schedule for New York. Anthony Richardson Sr. is facing quite the challenge as he makes his first start at quarterback since December 2024.

articles.title: NFL Exec Fears Burrows' Bengals, Would Rather Play Mahomes' Chiefs or Josh Allen's Bills
articles.summary: Before facing the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football, the Cincinnati Bengals appear to have already established themselves as the team to beat in the competitive AFC.
articles.body:
Before facing the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football, the Cincinnati Bengals appear to have already established themselves as the team to beat in the competitive AFC.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to multiple executives from other teams who picked the Bengals as the top team in the conference over perennial powerhouses like the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills.

"I would want to play Kansas City — I'd want to play Buffalo," one exec said. "I would not want to play Cincinnati. Dexter (Lawrence) in the middle of that defense would be difficult. He would cause a lot of issues to your run game. (Boye) Mafe is a really good piece."

Exec: Josh Allen 'Scariest Player Ever' 😱

"My gut is that Cincinnati's the best team in that group," another exec said.

The Bengals (7-2) haven't made the playoffs since 2022, but their improved defense this year has helped make them a balanced team that is capable of holding its own against elite squads. Star quarterback Joe Burrow leads the league with 27 passing touchdowns, outperforming Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes and Bills star Josh Allen.

Some still see the Chiefs as the top team in the AFC, thanks to their improved rushing attack behind Mahomes.

"Kansas City's battle-tested (in past seasons)," one exec said. "I just don't know if they have enough. We'll see how the receiving corps comes along, but they're probably the most balanced, especially if the running back (Kenneth Walker III) is full strength."

However, an opposing coach still gave the nod to the Bengals, pointing to their high-powered offense.

"Coaching-wise, Kansas City has a huge advantage relative to Cincinnati or Buffalo," the coach said. "But I look at Kansas City not doing great in special teams — lots to be desired there. And they don't have as much skill on offense as Cincinnati."

The Bengals will look to extend their win streak to six straight games when they meet the Commanders on Monday night

articles.title: NFL Exec Rips Jaguars After Loss to Giants, 'They Think They're All That, But They're Really Not'
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars' loss to the New York Giants on Sunday is already changing the way that those around the league perceive the team.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars' loss to the New York Giants on Sunday is already changing the way that those around the league perceive the team.

In Mike Sando 's story on Monday, he spoke to an NFC executive who ripped into the Jaguars.

"Jacksonville showed some vulnerability," an exec from an NFC team said in the story. "They think they're all that, but they're really not. They got out-physicaled, which was interesting."

Jacksonville lost 23-18 to the Giants on Sunday after kicking a late field goal down 8 and then not getting the ball back.

"I get the margin of victory and all that," a second NFC exec said, "but they almost lost to the Eagles in London, and really should have lost. They lost to Denver, beat Baltimore without Lamar (Jackson). I can still easily see them going 13-4, 14-3. Maybe they get the one seed, but they could (also) absolutely be knocked out in the first round."

Jacksonville fell to 7-3 with the loss and will look to bounce back in Week 12 against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: DK Metcalf escapes NFL suspension as Pittsburgh Steelers receiver denies poking Cooper DeJean in the eyes
articles.summary: DK Metcalf was ejected from the Pittsburgh Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after appearing to reach into Cooper DeJean's facemask and poke him in the eyes; the NFL will not suspend the receiver but he could be fined, according to sources
articles.body:
Metcalf denied that he intentionally stuck his fingers in the Eagles defender's facemask when addressing the media on Monday.

Having been ejected from a game for the third time in his career during the second half of the Steelers' 19-16 loss on Sunday, Metcalf initially said that he "couldn't remember" the incident, before backtracking and saying that he was trying to send a message to DeJean to "stop pushing me".

Metcalf had caught only one pass for two yards before being sent to the locker room after being flagged twice for personal fouls following a couple of confrontations with DeJean.

The NFL will review Metcalf's actions during the game for potential fines as part of its standard disciplinary review process, ESPN and NFL Network reported, but he escapes a suspension.

The 28-year-old was banned for two games last season for swiping at a fan in Detroit and was shown the door twice earlier in his career while playing for the Seattle Seahawks.

Asked why this keeps happening, Metcalf told reporters: "I think you got to ask the people that seem to do that to me".

Metcalf noted that opponents trying to get under his skin is nothing new, saying that San Francisco 49ers players attempted to do that regularly during the Seahawks' frequent meetings with their NFC West rivals.

The two-time Pro Bowler, who is on pace for career lows in receptions and yards receiving this season, declined to blame the heated interaction on frustration, pointing out that the Steelers are "winning", though Pittsburgh (6-4) has dropped two straight after losing in Philadelphia.

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy called Metcalf's actions "unacceptable" but said he needed more information before deciding whether to take any action.

Metcalf did not appear to be worried about being disciplined by the Steelers or the NFL. "You've got to ask [Pittsburgh general manager] Omar [Khan] that, or anybody else other than DeKaylin," Metcalf said, using his given name.

The highest-paid wide receiver in team history also added that the Steelers need to "score points when we get the ball and not stall on third down or get a turnover on downs, stay on the field so our defense can stay off the field".

Pittsburgh remain firmly in playoff position as Thanksgiving looms but face a daunting stretch over the next three weeks that includes a pair of meeting with first-placed teams in their division - the Denver Broncos (8-2) and Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), as well as a key clash with fellow AFC wildcard contenders the Houston Texans (4-6).

articles.title: Browns Called a 'Mirage' by NFL Exec amid Winning Record with Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders at QB
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have been one of the NFL's pleasant surprises this season, going 6-4 thus far and finding themselves firmly in the AFC playoff picture.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have been one of the NFL's pleasant surprises this season, going 6-4 thus far and finding themselves firmly in the AFC playoff picture.

Not everybody believes they are for real, however.

"Cleveland is a mirage (at 6-4), but otherwise, I feel like there is no out-of-nowhere team this year," an NFC executive told Mike Sando of The Athletic.

The Browns and their fans won't like the disrespect, of course. But Cleveland's only win against a team with a winning record this season came against the Pittsburgh Steelers, a 6-4 team that is currently riding a two-game losing streak. The Browns are 1-2 against teams with winning records thus far.

The schedule tightens up a bit down the stretch, with a pair of matchups against the Cincinnati Bengals and a game against the New York Giants. But in general, the Browns have a very manageable slate this season.

Stat Line : 18 of 31 for 155 yards and a touchdown

Josh Johnson may be the ultimate journeyman quarterback, but he's also a consummate professional. At 40 years old and signed to his NFL team, Johnson took over the Arizona Cardinals offense less than two weeks after joining the team.

With Carson Beck out with a back injury, Johnson didn't make any major mistakes but his transition to the starting lineup certainly set the Cardinals back. Arizona mustered only 205 yards.

It's difficult to dock the veteran quarterback considering the circumstances. At the same time, the Cardinals punted or turned the ball over one downs during their final seven offensive possessions.

"We made some plays here and there, and showed flashes," Johnson told reporters , "but flashes against good teams don't get you nothing."

Score : 35-33 loss vs. Carolina Panthers

Stat Line : 24 of 37 for 276 yard, a touchdown and an interception

Jacoby Brissett has kept the Baltimore Ravens competitive over the last two weeks, while showing exactly why he's a quality backup quarterback but not the answer as a team's starter.

During Sunday's matchup, the Ravens' meltdown during their final offensive possession, while trailing by two points with 1:44 left to play, was something to behold.

A sack, short checkdown pass and quarterback sneak on 4th-and-1 gave the Ravens a first down from their own 32-yard line with 36 seconds left. Brissett then avoided pressure, twirled around and heaved an ill-advised pass that resulted in the game-sealing interception. Brissett was supposed to provide a stabilizing presence, not make thew worst possible decision during a critical moment.

"I was trying to get it out of bounds," Brissett told reporters . "Did a poor job of that."

Stat Line : 27 of 45 for 304 yard, a touchdown and two interceptions

The final score between the Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins doesn't tell the whole story. The Dolphins haven't quit despite a 1-9 start. Miami's defensive front legitimately made life difficult on Bills quarterback Josh Allen.

"We picked them off twice, we hit them, we sacked them," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters . "We held them to a lot of field goals. Red-zone defense was pretty good. But just not enough to win." The Bills even failed to run for 100 yards as a team.

Allen responded by slipping through multiple would-be tacklers, avoiding pressure and extending plays when necessary. Plus, Buffalo's defense has been exceptional since the start of November, which gives Allen and the Bills' offense far more leeway than the unit has experienced in previous year.

Stat Line : 22 of 30 for 254 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers kept finding ways to come back against the Baltimore Ravens until they stood victorious in the end.

Baltimore built a 12-0 lead going into Sunday's second quarter. Carolina then scored 14 unanswered points. From there, the lead changed six times. Ultimately, Young led a 12-play drive that ended with the game-winning field goal.

"Game on the line, nobody else I want with the ball," Panthers head coach Dave Canales told reporters . "Bryce Young's going to go there. He's going to be, he's going to be in control. He's going to be focused, locked into the moment, and that's what he looked like on that drive."

While another game-winning drive is impressive, the Carolina quarterback's ability to respond while under constant duress became the more remarkable aspect of Young's performance. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Young completed 66.7 percent of his passes for a career-higher 173 yards when pressured.

Score : 21-13 win vs. New Orleans Saints

Stat Line : 15 of 23 for 181 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Caleb Williams won't be "on" every single weekend. Fortunately for the Chicago Bears, the team's defense has really reached a different stage since defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons joined the unit. Now, the Bears are playing complementary football and Williams doesn't need to provide an MVP-caliber performance during every outing.

Williams' 183 passing yards and the Bears' 21 points were the fewest in a win since last November.

"I think there was opportunity for a lot of points out there, whether it's us being on the same page, us being efficient running and efficient passing," Williams told reporters . "I think there was a lot more we left out there and a lot more we can be better at this week coming up."

Stat Line : 28 of 33 for 325 yards and four touchdowns; four carries for nine yards and a score

[Cue the famous "thinking" GIF .] The Dallas Cowboys defense doesn't need to stop an opponent when the team's offense scores on every possession (excluding the game-ending kneel-down). That's exactly what happened Sunday when the Cowboys scored 51 points, with seven touchdowns drives, including six straight to open the contest.

Dak Prescott was nearly flawless facing the Tennessee Titans defense. He had only one fewer touchdown pass compared to incomplete passes. The traditional pocket passer even ran for a score.

"Dak is just a special guy," wide receiver CeeDee Lamb told reporters . "He does that every week, the way he prepares. He was on his own time. They weren't moving him off his pivot and when they were, he was still composed. Dak just being the consistent leader he is, he makes it easy for us to go run through the wall for him."

Stat Line : 19 of 35 for 222 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Denver Broncos may finally be establishing an offensive identity, and it's less about Bo Nix taking on more responsibility. Instead, the team's ground game has seemingly awoken, with fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman leading the way. Coleman ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. This ground-based attack appears to be the biggest adjustment coming out of the Broncos' bye week.

"The approach that we're taking now, and the confidence that we're playing with, it's really about us," Coleman told reporters . "We look at ourselves in the mirror and know that we're the better team. We just have to play like it and execute like it. It's just the mindset of knowing we're better than you and, 'We don't care if you know we're running the ball, we're still going to run it.'"

Score : 31-21 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 20 of 28 for 279 yards and two touchdowns

With the Chicago Bears awaiting a Thanksgiving Day showdown, the Detroit Lions could have easily slipped up against the three-win Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Instead, the Lions handled business despite potential pitfalls.

"I think we had a good week of practice and felt really good with our plan, how we were going to try to attack them," Jared Goff told reporters . "It's a really good defense. They do a really good job at all three levels, and we had our hands full. I think they're so stout in the run game. … You kind of have to attack them in that way. It's certainly how we've done it the last few years when we've played them." To Goff's point, the quarterback benefited from another Jahmyr Gibbs standout performance. The league's leading rusher provided 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. To the Goff's credit, he returned to his normal efficient self and didn't throw an interception for the first time since the month of November began.

Stat Line : 21 of 27 for 197 yards, three touchdowns and an interception; six carries of 27 yards

CJ Stroud is on a roll and back to where everyone thought he'd be after a sterling rookie campaign. The fourth-year signal-caller has thrown for two or more touchdowns in five straight games, including three or more in four of those contests.

"C.J. is producing the way he is producing because of the work he put in throughout the offseason," Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters . "All of that is paying dividends now. He's been ready for these moments and he's been executing at a high level in these moments." The conversation is no longer about whether Stroud is holding back the team. It's shifted to whether he can place the squad on his shoulders and lead the Texans to a postseason berth after an 0-4 start. With multiple winnable games ahead, the latter remains possible.

Stat Line : 12 of 27 for 144 yards and an interception

The Indianapolis Colts released Daniel Jones a day after Thursday's embarrassing loss to the rival Houston Texans. Jones was only 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract extension he signed this past offseason. Does anything more to be said about badly things went for Jones and the Colts this season? Good luck, Anthony Richardson Sr. The 2023 fourth overall draft pick has six games to prove whether he can finally be the Colts' long-term answer at quarterback.

Stat Line : 25 of 47 for 301 yards, a touchdown and an interception

In order for the Jacksonville Jaguars to be taken seriously, they must show they're capable of handling quality opponents. They did not do so Sunday against the New York Giants. Instead, the Giants defense had Trevor Lawrence and Co. on their heels.

"He got rattled," Giants outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said of Lawrence . "He was taking some hits, so they definitely couldn't get on schedule."

New York sacked Lawrence three times and hit him on 11 different occasions. Lawrence clearly couldn't establish any rhythm, which led to his two interceptions. According to ESPN Insights , the Giants pressured Lawrence on 42 percent of his dropbacks. As a result, Lawrence wasn't nearly as accurate or comfortable working from the pocket and it showed.

Stat Line : 27 of 39 for 324 yards and three touchdowns

It's easy to forget that Patrick Mahomes suffered a significant knee injury to end his 2025 campaign, because he was in the lineup for the Kansas City Chiefs when the '26 season opened for business.

Every athlete needs time to adjust coming off a major injury, even one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time. Early in the season, Mahomes didn't play like his old self. Most of the Chiefs' passing attack fell within the short-to-intermediate zones.

The Mahomes magic has been rekindled in recent weeks. Since the calendar turned to November, the Chiefs' quarterback is averaging 309 passing yards per game, while posting a 13-to-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio.

"I'm excited for the rest of the season," Mahomes told reporters , "but it all begins Thursday night [against the Buffalo Bills]."

Stat Line : 18 of 37 for 267 yards, three touchdown and an interception; four carries for 22 yards

The Las Vegas Raiders offense faced a talented and stingy defense Sunday against the Denver Broncos. Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza responded after a slow start and opened eyes.

Trailing 17-0 in the second quarter, this year's No. 1 overall pick led the Raiders all the way back to tie the game before it finally got out of hand—which included a Mendoza pick-six. In doing so, the Broncos now know the Raiders won't be a pushover when the two teams face each again.

"There certainly was a lot of respect for Fernando Mendoza in the Broncos locker room," James Palmer reported . "What stood out was how calm he was in the pocket and his feel in the pocket, as well as how unpredictable he is when he starts to move. Most young players have something they do and go to it over and over again. Mendoza scrambles out a variety of ways and scans the field well while doing it."

Stat Line : 15 of 21 for 131 and two touchdowns; eight carries for 32 yards and a score

At this point, Justin Herbert should just throw his hands the air purely out of disgust. The New York Jets sacked Herbert six times. Despite that constant duress, Herbert continues to play better in recent weeks.

So much has been made about Mike McDaniel serving as the team's offensive coordinator this season that people forget it takes time for players to get comfortable within a new scheme.

"It's your first time together, your first time going through anything, attacking certain defenses, doing certain concepts," McDaniel said last week . "You just get a ton of feedback. That's always good because you have more information to move forward with. Inherently, there's going to be things that he likes and things that he's like, 'Ah, live, I didn't feel like I could see that the way I thought I'd be able to see it.' Got it."

Herbert has showed progress. The Chargers may still be counted among the league's worst teams, but the concern over whether their quarterback may be broken is no longer as much of a talking point.

Stat Line : 12 of 33 for 102 yards and an interception

The Miami Dolphins have reached the stage where a lost season weighs heavily on a team. The Dolphins are now 1-9. Quarterback Kyle McCord struggled mightily against the Buffalo Bills' surging defense. Miami won't leave Sunday's beatdown with much excitement about what comes next.

"Development is important to me," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters, "but these days are hard because we want to win. There is development going on, and I want our guys to also understand that we haven't been good enough today. ... We just gotta keep going."

McCord will remain at helm with Malik Willis on injured reserve, even after being overwhelmed by Jim Leonhard's unit. At the same time, Miami's surrounding cast did nothing to help McCord.

"We got to help him out... just watching him got out there and compete today, I got no issues with Kyle," Hafley added .

Score : 35-10 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 26 of 38 for 235 yards and an interception

The shoe was on the other foot during Sunday Night Football , because the San Francisco 49ers' defense, not the Minnesota Vikings' D, had their opponent in dire straights.

Kirk Cousins was clearly frustrated, and the Vikings offense couldn't get anything going during the second half, which is why Carson Wentz eventually entered the contest after Minnesota trailed by three scores.

"We didn't finish drives," Cousins told reporters . "Felt like there were too many drives that we're moving the football and then we stall out and don't get any points."

The Vikings scored only one redzone touchdown despite three trips inside San Francisco's 20-yard line. Plus, Minnesota finished a combined eight of 17 on third and fourth downs.

Stat Line : 25 of 42 for 222 yards, a touchdown and an interception; three carries for 34 yards

A flicker of something special can always be seen within the New Orleans Saints offense, yet the unit never fully ignites.

"There's a few minute details on certain plays that have cost us," Shough told reporters . "And that's really what it comes down to. It's frustrating, for sure." For Shough, he faced significant pressure Sunday against the Chicago Bears' talented defensive front. Chicago sacked Shough six times and hit the quarterback on 10 occasions. That scenario is difficult for anyone to overcome. At some point, the Saints need to piece it all together, because plenty of talent can be found within the team's offense. Otherwise, questions will start to be raised about the coaching staff, Shough leading the unit and what direction the team will ultimately go. At 3-7, New Orleans could realistically finish with a worse record than last season despite significant optimism surrounding this squad entering the current campaign.

Score : 27-24 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 17 of 21 for 176 yards and three touchdowns

The New York Jets have so much young talent that Geno Smith's bounce-back season gets overlooked to a degree. The reason likely centers on the fact Smith is viewed as a bridge to whichever quarterback the Jets draft next April. He's a placeholder. Though he's also performed better than expected this season.

Granted, both Smith and the Jets could have played better in recent weeks. Still, the veteran signal-caller completed over 80 percent of his passes Sunday, contributed three touchdowns and helped lead the Jets to a win against a cross-country opponent.

"For sure, I think we can build off of it," Smith told reporters . "I feel like I can play a whole lot better, so I'm focusing on pushing myself to get better every day, as well as the guys around me."

Score : 23-18 win vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 18 of 38 for 173 yards and a touchdown; seven carries for 33 yards

JJ McCarthy won't dispel any doubters with a performance like he provided Sunday despite the New York Giants' claiming a quality win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

McCarthy completed under 50 percent of his passes, while missing multiple open receivers. The quarterback's biggest play was when he made the tackle after a Jaguars' fumble recovery that could have turned into six points. Jacksonville didn't score on the ensuing drive.

"I was shocked (Antonio Johnson) wasn't looking at me when I was running down the field," McCarthy told reporters . "He was just looking forward and looking at the sideline. But at the end of the day, you have to do your job as a quarterback. When everything goes wrong, try to find a way to make it right."

Score : 19-16 win vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Joe Milton III may be the Philadelphia Eagles' third starting quarterback this season, but head coach Nick Sirianni wouldn't allow that distinction to hold back his offense during a critical moment.

Milton has always been an example of a quarterback packed with potential yet lacked polish. Sirianni and his staff placed the ball in Milton's hands on a critical 3rd-and-6 situation to put the game away, which resulted in a seven-yard pass-and-catch to DeVonta Smith.

"You want to be aggressive in four-minute situations," Sirianni told reporters . "... Smitty did a good job running the route and catching the ball. Joe delivered it right there."

The outcome in that situation is impressive considering Milton and Smith were playing their first game together.

Score : 19-16 loss vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : 30 of 44 for 227 yards and a touchdown; five carries for 29 yards

The aging Aaron Rogers has gone from the game's best deep-ball thrower to Captain Checkdown. However, the long-time starter continued career-long trend of pass-aggressive leadership instead of looking at his own shortcomings.

"He called for more interaction," CBS Sports' Melanie Collins reported (h/t Steelers Depot ). "He said it's tough nowadays with these iPads. Back in the day, you could check guys' notes and make sure they were writing things down. It almost felt like he was calling out the guys a little bit for a lack of details. He wants everyone to feel like they're contributing to what's happening on game day, even when they're not on the field."

The Steelers have issues at wide receiver. However, the majority of the offense and Rodgers' passes are at, behind or near the line of scrimmage. Rodgers' effectiveness when trying the push the ball downfield has dropped off dramatically.

Stat Line : 21 of 26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns

The San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy looked at the Minnesota Vikings and presumably thought to himself, "What great defense?"

The Vikings were relentless in their approach to pressure Purdy. The Niners quarterback didn't blink, though.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Purdy completed 16 of 18 passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns when Minnesota blitzed. He completed eight of nine passes when actually pressured. The 26-year-old veteran played decisively and led the Niners to a touchdown on their of their first four offensive possessions.

"Our quarterback was unbelievable," head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters . "You can't hesitate versus those guys. You got to let it rip. And he continually did that over and over while protecting the ball."

Stat Line : 20 of 33 for 187 yards and two touchdowns; six carries for 36 yards

No one will ever question Baker Mayfield's toughness. At the same time, questions should be raised about his effectiveness, especially when he's playing through an injury.

Mayfield is currently dealing with a heel injury. He did throw a pair of touchdowns Sunday, though one came once the game was out of hand.

To Mayfield's credit, he gutted out a performance where Tampa Bay remained competitive well into the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers allowing touchdowns during the Detroit's final two offensive possessions (not including a kneel-down) took the ball out of the quarterback's hands and led to Tampa's seventh loss this season.

"We made some plays, but we didn't quite make enough," Mayfield told reporters . "That's frustrating because we can do all of this in practice, but we haven't been able to translate that to Sundays yet."

Stat Line : 21 of 30 for 248 yards and two touchdowns

Cam Ward fought an uphill battle from the start of Sunday's contest against the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys scored and never stopped scoring. The Titans defense allowed 480 yards and never made a play to break serve.

Granted, Ward and the Titans offense could have played better during the first half when the game was still within reach. Tennessee matched touchdowns with field goals, which didn't help matters. But that same group came out and scored back-to-back touchdowns in the third quarter trying to match what turned out to be the unstoppable Cowboys.

"Control what we can control," Ward told reporters . "Continue to back the defense up. Continue to bring them life by scoring the football. We didn't have our best day today. We got stalled out in the red zone a couple of times. We had a turnover. At the end of the day, we've all got to help each other out."

articles.title: 8 Bargain Free Agents That Contenders Should Sign For 2026 NFL Playoff Push
articles.summary: As we enter the final stretch of the 2026 NFL season, teams can add free agents to fuel a playoff run. As is the case every year, roster attrition takes its toll, creating a need for reinforcements.
articles.body:
As we enter the final stretch of the 2026 NFL season, teams can add free agents to fuel a playoff run. As is the case every year, roster attrition takes its toll, creating a need for reinforcements.

This late in the season, it's hard to fill key spots on the depth chart with quality talent, but experienced veterans can be an ideal fit for a short stint.

Looking at the top eight available free agents, here are potential landing spots where they can help contenders make a playoff push. These team-player pairings are mostly based on roster need, though schematic fit is also a determining factor.

The Jacksonville Jaguars lost left tackle Anton Harrison for the season after he tore his ACL in early October. In their previous game against the New York Giants, Harrison's replacement, Walker Little, suffered a knee injury.

If Little is out for an extended period, the Jaguars will need to protect quarterback Trevor Lawrence's blind side.

Last Sunday, the Giants consistently pressured Lawrence, who took three sacks in a loss. Other teams will look at that game and likely try to emulate what Big Blue did to rattle Lawrence in the pocket, and it would be easier to do that against a third-string left tackle.

Taylor Decker is a 10-year starter who would fit the Jaguars' need at left tackle if the team must choose another fill-in replacement. Last year, with the Detroit Lions, he allowed just two sacks over 551 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus .

In Week 10, Detroit Lions edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack. Edge-rusher D.J. Wonnum and defensive tackle Alim McNeil have seven and 6.5 sacks, respectively.

Yet the Lions should bring in a veteran pass rusher to complement rookie second-rounder Derrick Moore, who's played 35 percent of the defensive snaps this season.

Moore has seen an uptick in snaps lately, though he could hit a proverbial rookie wall late in the season. With the addition of a battle-tested veteran like Leonard Floyd, the Lions would increase their chance of maintaining a top-12 pressure rate at 24 percent .

At 34, Floyd is best suited as a designated pass-rusher, though he can still be effective in a rotation.

In 2025, with the Atlanta Falcons, Floyd recorded 19 tackles (five for loss), 3.5 sacks and 19 pressures while on the field for 49 percent of the defensive snaps in 15 starts.

DB C.J. Gardner-Johnson: Kansas City Chiefs

The Kansas City Chiefs addressed their biggest need at the trade deadline, acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts, though they can still upgrade the back end of the defense.

Kansas City will likely face prolific aerial attacks in the playoffs. In the AFC, the Cincinnati Bengals, Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills all field top-12 passing offenses. Although the Chiefs rank seventh in total pass defense, that unit hasn't faced a passing offense better than the Las Vegas Raiders' 11th-ranked unit so far this season.

The Chiefs should add C.J. Gardner-Johnson ahead of a playoff run. He can be volatile on the field, but the eighth-year pro is a versatile defensive back who can play multiple roles in the secondary. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo can be creative with him in coverage.

Also, with 21 career interceptions in 93 games (77 starts), Gardner-Johnson could be a game-changer in critical playoff situations.

The New York Giants need at least one more capable ball-carrier to spark their 19th-ranked rushing attack. Entering Week 12, Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary are the only notable running backs on their active roster. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve. The club has elevated Phil Mafah from the practice squad twice, but he hasn't logged a carry this season.

In Big Blue's previous outing, Skattebo lost a fumble late in the third quarter. Keep in mind the Giants benched the bruising ball-carrier in Week 6 because of his ball-security issues, which makes you wonder whether they fully trust him in a workhorse role.

With Tracy having two fumbles this season, the Giants should circle back to Antonio Gibson, whom they worked out last week.

If Gibson is fully recovered from a torn ACL suffered in October of last season, the Giants should consider adding him to a platoon with Skattebo, Singletary and Tracy when he returns from injured reserve.

In six seasons with the New England Patriots and Washington Commanders, Gibson recorded 787 carries for 3,287 yards and 24 touchdowns. He can also be an asset on passing downs, with 197 catches for 1,495 yards and seven touchdowns.

Still in his prime at 28, Gibson could boost the Giants' muddled backfield.

The Los Angeles Rams have to take a tough path to the playoffs without their top two wide receivers.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Puka Nacua will miss the rest of the season after undergoing MCL surgery, and Davante Adams is a "long shot" to return in Week 13 from hamstring surgery.

No matter how many tight ends head coach Sean McVay plans to use without his key pass-catchers, the Rams desperately need help at wide receiver. So, they should try to sign the best one available.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Tyreek Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, was in contact with multiple clubs, with the goal of the wide receiver "being on a team in the immediate future."

Hill underwent multiple surgeries on his knee after suffering season-ending injuries in September of last year. If he returns this season, the Rams could use him in a featured role until Adams comes back.

Even if Hill has lost some of his explosiveness, he would be an upgrade over Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured fibula and is expected to miss six weeks, which makes his return for the season uncertain.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Patriots are expected to start Tommy DeVito, though the team will explore the free-agent market. Head coach Mike Vrabel said DeVito is "our starter" on Monday, but it would help to have an insurance policy if the backup struggles.

If Daniel Jones clears waivers, the Patriots should be a prime landing spot for him. Despite his shortcomings with the Indianapolis Colts, he would be an upgrade over DeVito, who has started eight games in four seasons.

In a shocking move, the Colts released Jones after keeping him past the trade deadline.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Baltimore Ravens, without Lamar Jackson, offered Indianapolis a fourth-round pick for Jones and a conditional fifth-round pick; the Minnesota Vikings also expressed interest.

Seen as a viable starter, Jones could keep the Patriots' playoff hopes alive. This year, he's thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions with a 58.4 percent completion rate, but the eighth-year veteran has had solid seasons with the New York Giants and Colts before tearing his Achilles.

In the short term, Jones would be a solid signing for a 5-5 team battling for a playoff spot.

Leading up to the November 10 trade deadline, analysts linked the Cincinnati Bengals to cornerbacks on the market. The Bengals backed out of a trade for edge-rusher Arnold Ebiketie and didn't make any moves.

In a position to win the AFC North, the Bengals should be aggressive in filling roster holes as they were this past offseason when they acquiring three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II from the New York Giants.

Now, with a chance to get back to the Super Bowl with a red-hot offense, the Bengals can bolster their defense by adding Haason Reddick.

Reddick can fill a void in the Bengals' pass rush while rookie second-rounder Cashius Howell recovers from wrist surgery. He can also strengthen Cincinnati's contain against the run. The Bengals are allowing five yards per carry.

Reddick appeared in 13 games (12 starts) with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season, recording 31 tackles (six for loss), 2.5 sacks and eight pressures while on the field for 71 percent of the defensive snaps. At 32, he's still a three-down defender who can play a vital role on the edge.

The Detroit Lions should consider double-dipping on available free agents. In addition to a pass rusher to replace Aidan Hutchinson, they may also need a linebacker if All-Pro Jack Campbell remains out for the long term.

In Week 8, Campbell suffered a neck injury that hospitalized him. Head coach Dan Campbell received " positive " news about the linebacker's condition, but the team doesn't have a timetable for a potential return.

The Lions can solidify their front seven by signing six-time first-team All-Pro linebacker Bobby Wagner.

At 36, Wagner can still perform at a high level. He last suited up for the Washington Commanders in 2025, logging 162 tackles (eight for loss), 4.5 sacks and 11 pressures while allowing an 89 passer rating in coverage.

Wagner's production and leadership qualities can be the glue for the Lions defense in a potential playoff run.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.
