articles.title: B/R Experts Week 12 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We have made it 11 weeks into the 2026 NFL season, and the playoff chase is in full swing.
articles.body:
We have made it 11 weeks into the 2026 NFL season, and the playoff chase is in full swing.

In some divisions, that chase is already all but over. After rolling in Week 11, the San Francisco 49ers (NFC West) and Buffalo Bills (AFC East) are running away with their divisions. The New York Giants (NFC East) and Carolina Panthers (NFC South) have surprisingly built sizable leads in their divisions. The Jacksonville Jaguars stumbled last week, but barring a total collapse the AFC South is theirs.

However, some divisions are far from settled. The NFC North has the makings of a true brouhaha over the regular season stretch run—all four teams have at least six wins. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos both sit atop the AFC West at 8-2.

With seven weeks to go in the regular season, for everything that appears settled in the NFL there's something that isn't—the league is in constant flux. And just as they do every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to examine the league's latest happenings and rank the NFL's teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Week 11 Result : Lost vs. New York Jets 27-24

Welp, the Los Angeles Chargers couldn't string together back-to-back wins and fell to 1-9 after Sunday's loss to the New York Jets. At this point, questions must be raised whether an organizational reset is necessary after this season.

Jim Harbaugh may be a high-profile head coach, but this season has been an absolute disaster. This year's campaign will be his first losing season as a head coach since he was at Stanford. He turns 63 in a month. Quarterback Justin Herbert looks like a shell of himself. The Chargers lack all of the traits that usually define Harbaugh-led squads. Yes, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel turned out to be a terrible fit, but Harbaugh hired him.

A fresh start as the team stares down a two-three pick in the 2027 NFL draft may be exactly what the Chargers need instead of hoping this will eventually turn around, which doesn't seem like it's going to happen anytime soon. -- Sobleski

Things went as expected for the Miami Dolphins in Week 11. The talent-starved team was forced to start backup quarterback Kyle McCord for the second straight week and was up against the current front-runner for the AFC's No. 1 seed.

Miami's defense did its best to keep things respectable, repeatedly forcing the Buffalo Bills to settle for field goals. Unfortunately, the Dolphins couldn't get enough out of their offense to keep pace on the scoreboard. That's not an issue that suddenly appeared with McCord in the lineup.

Starter Malik Willis, who is on IR with a groin injury, does offer a scrambling element that McCord does not. However, Miami has lacked the offensive firepower needed to take advantage when the defense has kept things close.

Due to a lackluster supporting cast and the injury, the Dolphins may still not know what they have in Willis by the end of the regular season. -- Knox

Back in March, the Indianapolis Colts signed quarterback Daniel Jones to a two-year, $88 million contract that included $50 million in guarantees. Just over eight months later, Jones was cut—released after a catastrophic effort against the Texans Thursday night.

While speaking to reporters , head coach Shane Steichen said that Indy's dismal season, wasn't entirely Jones' fault.

"There's a lot of factors," Steichen said. "I don't think it was just on one person. I think there's a lot of factors that played into it. Obviously, the quarterback takes a lot of the blame. Obviously, that's the business that we're in. But things just didn't work out."

Jones has been truly terrible this year—he's the first quarterback in 45 years to start in each of his team's first 11 games of a season without recording a single game where he had more passing touchdowns than interceptions.

But Steichen's right—this entire franchise has imploded. – Davenport

After allowing over 50 points on the road at Dallas Sunday, the Titans are insured of a fifth straight losing season—the longest such streak since the team moved to Tennessee in 1997.

It was an ugly outing in which the Titans gave up 480 yards of offense and were just two-for-five in the red zone offensively. After the loss, head coach Robert Saleh was obviously displeased by the effort while talking to reporters .

"There's a lot of things that need to change," Saleh said. "Obviously it's disgusting football. It's embarrassing football. And obviously that starts with me."

For those searching for silver linings, Titans quarterback Cam Ward had his third straight solid game, throwing two touchdown passes and running for another. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate caught one of those scores.

But since trading away defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons and safety Amani Hooker, the Titans defense has been non-existent. -- Davenport

Week 11 Result: Lost at Kansas City 34-7

It has officially gotten ugly for the Arizona Cardinals.

Sure, expectations were low Sunday at Arrowhead. The Redbirds are on their fourth starting quarterback of the season. The wide receiver room is a who's who of "who?" But that doesn't erase the sting of a second straight loss by at least 27 points. Over the last three games, Arizona has scored 16 points—total.

While speaking to the media, first-year head coach Mike LaFleur allowed that it has been a rough stretch—and at this points the season is about salvaging some respect down the stretch.

"It's been one helluva stretch for us. It's been one helluva stretch really since Week 2," said LaFleur. We've done some good, but more bad. But we have six weeks left."

Odds are Carson Beck isn't the long term answer under center in the desert. So frankly the last thing the Cardinals should want right now is to win meaningless games. -- Davenport

The good news for the New Orleans Saints is that their defense has continued to show signs of improvement since the Week 8 bye. The bad news is that New Orleans is just 1-2 since its break and still has one of the worst statistical units on the season.

The worse news is that the Saints seem to be a bit rudderless in their second season under head coach Kellen Moore.

The Saints had plenty of reasons for optimism at the end of last season. Quarterback Tyler Shough looked like a future star, and New Orleans rattled off four wins in their last five games. While Shough has continued to play like a franchise quarterback this season, the rest of the team has failed to show any tangible growth since last year.

At 3-7, the Saints are still alive in a mediocre division, but it's still hard to envision them in the postseason this year. -- Knox

The New York Jets aren't a good team overall, and it's hard to imagine that head coach Aaron Glenn will survive the season. However, they're doing a great job of laying the foundation for their next quarterback of the future.

With three 2027 first-round picks, New York is poised to add a promising quarterback prospect in the spring.

On Sunday, the Jets leaned on their ascending backfield duo of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. missed the game with ankle and hip injuries, but the Jets have plenty of capable pass-catchers—including Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Kenyon Sadiq, and Mason Taylor.

New York also has a solid bridge quarterback in Geno Smith, who will probably be worth re-signing in the offseason. Since one of those three 2027 first-rounders is coming from Indianapolis, Jets fans don't have to worry if their team picks up another win or two over the final six games. -- Knox

Week 11 Result: Won vs. Pittsburgh 19-16

The Philadelphia Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak, indicating they haven't given up on the season, though the playoffs are realistically out of reach.

The Eagles can still be stout defensively. They've allowed fewer than 20 points in their last two games, separated by a bye week.

Offensively, Philadelphia must define backup quarterback Joe Milton's ceiling. Next year, he could be the primary backup or a fill-in starter, depending on Jalen Hurts' recovery timeline from blood clots and whether the team allows Tanner McKee to sign elsewhere in free agency. -- Moton

In his first year as the Cleveland Browns' head coach in 2020, Kevin Stefanski led his team to the playoffs. In his first season as the Atlanta Falcons' head coach, he's leading his team toward a top-10 draft selection.

Continuing on the current path may ultimately be a good thing for the Falcons, as their lack of reliable quarterback play has been their biggest issue in 2026. That issue was particularly glaring over the past couple of weeks during blowout losses against Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes.

Michael Penix Jr. has shown a few flashes this season, but he's done nothing that should force Atlanta to ignore the 2027 quarterback class.

However, the Falcons aren't out of the NFC South mix just yet. Despite carrying just three wins into Thanksgiving week, they can still make a playoff run, especially if they manage to steal one against the Minnesota Vikings next week. -- Knox

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dropped their seventh game of the season on Sunday, though they're still very much alive in the NFC South. Tampa is 2-0 in divisional play and will host the Carolina Panthers on Monday night.

A win will put Tampa just one game behind Carolina with the head-to-head tiebreaker. What's unknown is whether Tampa can win that game and string together enough victories to actually claim the division.

The Bucs' defense has been terrific at stopping the run and forcing turnovers, and the offense can chew up yards in bunches on the ground. However, Baker Mayfield has been banged-up for most of the season, and Tampa has struggled to identify reliable go-to receivers.

If Tampa can figure out how to get its passing attack off the ground, it could push into the postseason and be a tough out in January. -- Knox

The Baltimore Ravens can probably forget about the playoffs and the possibility that Lamar Jackson returns from thumb surgery to save them.

A little over a week ago, head coach Jesse Minter released a statement that noted Jackson will be out six to 10 weeks.

By the front end of Jackson's recovery timetable, Baltimore may be out of postseason contention. On a six-game losing streak, the Ravens are their own worst enemy, with 12 turnovers over their last four games. – Moton

At 3-5-1, the Commanders are still clinging to the hope they can get back into the NFC East race. But let's be blunt. Washington ranks in the bottom half of the league in both total offense and total defense. They have yet to win consecutive games in 2026. No run is coming.

The Commanders are admittedly unlikely to beat the red-hot Bengals Monday night. But after that comes a month of sub-.500 opponents, including the one-win Titans and floundering Cardinals at home.

It's a slim chance. But it's there. -- Moton

The Las Vegas Raiders have lost both games in which Fernando Mendoza started. Yet, the resiliency seen from this year's No. 1 overall draft pick has been impressive.

The Denver Broncos built a 17-0 lead Sunday. Mendoza is going to have his ups and downs, of course. At the same time, the rookie signal-caller led his team to 17 straight points before everything started to fall apart again. In doing so, he opened some eyes among the Raiders' division rival.

"There certainly was a lot of respect for Fernando Mendoza in the Broncos locker room," James Palmer reported . "What stood out was how calm he was in the pocket and his feel in the pocket, as well as how unpredictable he is when he starts to move. Most young players have something they do and go to it over and over again. Mendoza scrambles out a variety of ways and scans the field well while doing it." -- Sobleski

Week 11 Result: Won vs. Indianapolis 26-3

Mind you, boatracing an imploding Indianapolis Colts team isn't exactly a Herculean task. But Houston won a game they needed to in order to remain on the fringes of playoff contention.

Whether the Texans make the playoffs or not, quarterback C.J. Stroud appears to have earned a second contract. After a fifth game in the last seven with a passer rating north of 100, Stroud told reporters he hopes to finish the season strong and get the Texans into the postseason for a fourth straight year.

"Always things you can clean up so we'll do that when the time is necessary," he said, "but I think you got to enjoy it, and it will be a couple of good weeks for us, so we got to go 1-0 mentality the rest of the time."

Houston won nine straight to make the playoffs last year after a 3-5 start. It will take a similar run this year—the Texans can afford maybe one more loss the rest of the way. – Davenport

The New England Patriots have been one of the biggest disappointments in the NFL this season, but perhaps we should have seen it coming.

New England played the league's third-easiest schedule in 2025. While the Patriots did survive through the playoffs to reach Super Bowl LX, they didn't quite like the same dominant team that largely dominated during the regular season.

Facing the league's sixth-hardest schedule in 2026, the Patriots have looked a lot more like the team that struggled through the postseason and lost badly in the Super Bowl.

After adding in the Super Bowl hangover and several key injuries, everything adds up to a lost season for New England. Drake Maye is likely done for the year with a fractured fibula, and prized trade acquisition A.J. Brown is set to miss multiple games with a hamstring injury. The Patriots are not getting back to the Super Bowl this year. -- Knox

As you would expect, the Dallas Cowboys offense looked like a well-oiled machine against the Tennessee Titans, though for the first time in a while, they put together a near-complete game with a takeaway and red-zone stops defensively.

The Titans scored a late garbage-time touchdown, but under new play-caller Mike Pettine, a senior defensive assistant on the coaching staff, the Cowboys put together a solid defensive outing they can build on.

The Cowboys' defense still has a lot to prove, but it's an underachieving unit that may have its best football ahead. -- Moton

It feels like the Carolina Panthers may win the NFC South by default. However, that doesn't mean that Carolina should be viewed as a major threat in the NFC.

The Panthers survived against the Ravens in Baltimore's second game with trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. Carolina's defense seemingly did its best to give the game away, allowing 421 yards and 33 points.

It was a major step backward for a defense that had shown signs of life since the firing of coordinator Ejiro Evero. Fortunately, the Panthers were able to trust Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard, and their offense to deliver the last and most important score of a back-and-forth game.

Carolina is back to .500 for the first time since Week 7 and can pick up a critical divisional win in Tampa Bay next Monday night. -- Knox

Week 11 Result: Lost at Philadelphia 19-16

The Pittsburgh Steelers entered their Week 9 bye on a four-game winning streak and lost momentum in back-to-back losses. They were blown out in a divisional matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals and struggled to move the ball in a loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Pittsburgh has scored fewer than 19 points in consecutive outings. Following last Sunday's game, head coach Mike McCarthy called out wideout DK Metcalf for getting ejected. Keep in mind the league suspended him for the final two games of the previous season after an altercation with a fan in Detroit.

The Steelers need Roman Wilson, who returned from injured reserve for the previous game, Michael Pittman Jr., who's still on injured reserve, and rookie third-rounder Germie Bernard to lead their passing attack. Metcalf needs to grow up, and the Steelers offense has to find its rhythm. -- Moton

The Cleveland Browns are earning their respect by winning close games. All six of their wins are by four points or fewer. While those contests could've gone the other way, they're battle-tested and won't flinch in coin-flip contests down the stretch.

To crack the top 10 in these power rankings, the Browns need to be more productive on offense. They're 18th in passing and 24th in rushing. Cleveland doesn't do anything particularly well on that side of the ball and must improve in both areas. -- Moton

Week 11 Result: Won vs. Jacksonville 23-18

The New York Giants notched a signature win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, but their offense raises some concerns.

Running back Cam Skattebo lost a fumble, and J.J. McCarthy completed only 47 percent of his pass attempts, moving the ball 4.6 yards per completion.

The last time Skattebo gave up a crucial possession, the Giants benched him the following week, but Big Blue doesn't have the available options to do that again. Since then, the club has released Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve.

Skattebo has ball-security issues, and McCarthy's ball placement can be erratic for stretches. The Giants defense has to carry this team while it works through offensive inefficiencies. – Moton

The Green Bay Packers enjoyed their bye this past weekend. Well, sort of.

Due to the holiday season, the Packers were somewhat robbed of the extra relaxation time, because they're playing on Thanksgiving Eve--which means the team didn't get a full week to decompress. Instead, only 10 days will pass between their latest games.

"When you don't have it as one big block and breaking it up doesn't necessarily, it's not the same as having a week off but I mean it is what it is, you got to embrace it and move on but obviously still take advantage of both breaks and give the body and mind a little reset," wide receiver Christian Watson told reporters . – Sobleski

The hits just keep coming for the Los Angeles Rams.

Entering the season, the Rams were the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI. But Los Angeles has been hit hard by injuries all season long. First edge-rusher Myles Garrett needed knee surgery. Then wide receiver Davante Adams tore his hamstring. Now Puka Nacua's season is over after he needed surgery to repair an MCL injury.

While talking to reporters , quarterback Matthew Stafford said the Rams are just going to have to do the best with what they have.

"(I've) played enough football that what matters is what you do on Sundays between the lines, and who can stay healthy, get healthy at the right times--all those kind of things," he said. "Find ways to win football games."

The Rams have done just that over the last month. But the schedule post-bye is brutal, and right now the Rams may well be more likely to miss the postseason altogether than play in another Super Bowl at home this year. – Davenport

The Seattle Seahawks aren't exactly where they expected to be after a bumpy start to the season, but at 6-4 the defending champs are in the playoff hunt. They also have an unexpected quarterback controversy—with a struggling Sam Darnold sidelined, Drew Lock has played well enough that some have questioned whether he should remain the starter even when Darnold is healthy.

To Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner, that question has an easy answer—no.

"This is probably the best I've seen Drew Lock play in his career," Warner said on The Rich Eisen Show . "(But) when you've got a guy that just won you a Super Bowl, he's played against tough competition, had some ups and downs, and hasn't necessarily been great this year, but you go back to that guy."

Next week's trip to San Francisco is Seattle's biggest test of the season to date. Win, and the NFC race actually is one down the stretch. Lose, and the division is no longer the priority.

Making the postseason at all is. -- Davenport

Week 11 Result: Lost at San Francisco 35-10

Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers unequivocally proved the Minnesota Vikings can't rely solely on their defense to be successful. A great team with an outstanding offensive scheme can overcome Brian Flores' mad scientist-caliber pressure packages. Once that happened, the Vikings had no answer.

San Francisco generated 343 offensive yards and scored touchdowns on three of their first four possessions. Also, Brock Purdy led a 13-play, 98-yard drive in the fourth quarter, too, which shouldn't be possible with how well Minnesota's defense had been playing.

Conversely, the Vikings offense struggled in the red zone and committed a pair of turnovers. Ultimately, the NFL's best teams will have answers for Minnesota's defense. Kevin O'Connell and Kirk Cousins need to have the same type of connection when the Vikings possess the ball. Otherwise, the team won't go very far beyond a postseason appearance. -- Sobleski

Week 11 Result : Won vs. Tampa Bay 31-21

Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury was a significant blow to the 8-2 Detroit Lions, especially in the NFC North where every team holds a winning record and any slip up could cause one of those squads to take a significant step back. However, the Lions defense--which had been a sore spot to start the season--has been mostly excellent since the team's Week 6 bye.

Detroit's offensive excellence is a given at this point. Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown are going to get theirs each week. It often falls on the Lions' defense to ensure the team doesn't find itself in a shootout. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers managed just 274 yards Sunday. More importantly, Detroit was able to generate pressure.

Rookie Derrick Moore was in on another sack. He now has 4.5 sacks over the last three games. DJ Wonnum played well coming off the other edge, registering his own sack. Plus, the Lions linebackers also got in on the act. Lest everyone forgets, Jack Campbell is still recovering from his injury, too. Yet, somehow, the Lions defense becomes more reliable with each passing week. -- Sobleski

Week 11 Result: Lost at New York Giants 23-18

Even the best of teams stub their toe every now and again. It happens. And maybe that's all Sunday's sloppy loss in New York was just a one-off. A bump in the road on the way to a deep playoff run.

But this was the second loss in three games this season on the road against a team with a winning record at the time. Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a pair of picks in one of his more uneven performances of the year. The Jags rushed for just 77 yards as a team. They also committed 13 penalties for over 100 yards.

Barring an epic collapse, the Jaguars are going to run away with the AFC South, and just two of their last seven opponents sport winning records.

But a Week 13 trip to Chicago now looms larger on the schedule.

Because the Jags need to show they can beat a good team on the road. -- Davenport

An argument can be made that the Cincinnati Bengals are the AFC's best team, even if few are really talking about them that way.

As we saw in last week's blowout win over the Steelers, the Bengals offense is as powerful as any in the game. Joe Burrow is playing like the MVP. Ja'Marr Chase is unstoppable. And while the Bengals defense may not be great, it's as good as it was the last time Cincy went to SoFi for a Super Bowl.

After Pittsburgh's stumble, the Bengals are two losses clear of every team in the division. But they need to win the games they are supposed to—like Monday night's trip to D.C. -- Moton

A different-looking Kansas City Chiefs offense opened the 2026 season, with running back Kenneth Walker III serving as the unit's focal point. Walker wasn't in the lineup Sunday and two things became blatantly clear in his absence.

First, Patrick Mahomes is fully back from last year's knee injury. It's easy to forget that the future Hall of Fame quarterback suffered his first major injury to end the 2025 campaign, because he opened this season in the lineup. However, the Chiefs off is revving up in recent weeks. Mahomes has averaged over 300 passing yards per game during Kansas City's last four outings, while providing a 13-to-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio.

Walker is a special back. The Chiefs appear to have another in rookie Emmett Johnson. The first-year ball-carrier has now posted back-to-back 100-yard games, with 314 yards from scrimmage in those contests.

Don't look now, but the Chiefs are rounding back into Super Bowl form. -- Sobleski

The Denver Broncos have leaned heavily on the same formula throughout the last two seasons: Let the defense go to work and allow Bo Nix to heat up late after a slow start. Sunday's outcome against the Las Vegas Raiders was slightly different but still somewhat concerning.

Denver made sure it wasn't a one-score game late in the contest. Though second-half stagnation allowed the Raiders to tie the game at one point. The biggest concern is opponents continue to outgain the Broncos. Eventually, better opposition is going to make Denver pay when they can move the ball far more effectively. Everyone may have to wait until Christmas Day to find out since that's when the Broncos face the Buffalo Bills.

At 8-2, the Broncos are counted among the league's best squads. It's debatable whether they actually belong there. -- Sobleski

Week 11 Result: Won vs. New Orleans 21-13

Trades made prior to the NFL deadline don't often live up to the hype. Jeffery Simmons has been everything the Chicago Bears hoped he would be and more.

Simmons registered three sacks and six more quarterback pressures Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. The six pressures tied for the most by a defensive tackle in a single game this season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . The 29-year-old veteran also adds significant flexibility to the Bears' defensive front. Simmons can move up and down the line of scrimmage, find favoriable one-on-one matchups and exploit them.

Chicago's success this season has been primarily built off the team's ability to move the ball with quarterback Caleb Williams orchestrating Ben Johnson's offense. The Bears' offense wasn't on point Sunday. Simmons and Co. were more than capable of picking up the slack. -- Sobleski

The Bills avoided any potential trap against the rival Dolphins on Sunday. It was another underwhelming game by Josh Allen, who threw a pair of picks, but Buffalo did enough on both sides of the ball to run away with a three-score win.

The challenges are about to get a lot tougher for the Bills, though. Buffalo's remaining schedule includes games against the Chiefs, Packers, Bears, and Broncos.

We'll find out in the coming weeks just what this Buffalo team is made of. Allen is obviously an MVP-caliber player when he's at his best, and the Bills have been getting enough out of their skill players. Buffalo's defense has also looked fantastic since the Week 7 bye, but there's a caveat there.

The Bills' defense has essentially played against a backup quarterback in 13 of 16 quarters since the bye. On Thursday, it will face Patrick Mahomes. -- Knox

Week 11 Result: Won vs. Minnesota 35-10 (Mexico City)

Sunday night's Mexico City beatdown was a statement win in every way—chief among them the statement that the 49ers are the NFL's best team. Period.

This was supposed to be a titanic showdown of the NFC's two one-loss teams. The Niners apparently didn't get that memo, because they took the Vikings behind the cobertizo para leña from the jump.

On the first drive of the game, it took San Francisco less than four minutes to drive the length of the field on one of the NFL's best defenses. Just before halftime a pick-six by the San Fran defense put the game on ice.

Brock Purdy is the NFL's MVP after 11 weeks. Given all the injuries the team has weathered on both sides of the ball, Kyle Shanahan is the Coach of the Year.

articles.title: New 49ers Rumors Uncover John Lynch Contract Extension Amid 9-1 Record in 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: After improving to 9-1 this season following Sunday's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, the San Francisco 49ers reportedly rewarded general manager John Lynch.
articles.body:
After improving to 9-1 this season following Sunday's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, the San Francisco 49ers reportedly rewarded general manager John Lynch.

Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that Lynch has agreed to a contract extension with the 49ers, with Lynch and team owner Jed York shaking hands prior to Monday night's game:

Lynch was hired as San Francisco's GM in 2017. He added the title of president of football operations in 2023. He's one of the most successful members of the player-turned-executive club, having played 15 seasons in the NFL with nine Pro Bowl selections before earning a Hall of Fame induction as part of the class of 2021.

During his tenure with the 49ers, Lynch has helped build the team into a perennial title contender. His partnership with head coach Kyle Shanahan has shaped the direction of the organization, and the future appears to be bright.

San Francisco owns the best record in the NFC, extending its win streak to three straight games after defeating Minnesota. The team ranks second in the NFL with 394.1 total yards per game and sixth with 309.8 total yards allowed per game, achieving balance on both sides of the ball.

Lynch's leadership has proven to be a key to the 49ers' success, and they will try to keep up the positive vibes when they return to action on Sunday in an NFC West matchup against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4).

articles.title: Cowboys' Christian Parker-Mike Pettine's Relationship Addressed by Kenny Clark After Major Change
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker wasn't thrilled to cede the play-calling to Mike Pettine, but the two have apparently maintained a cohesive partnership.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker wasn't thrilled to cede the play-calling to Mike Pettine, but the two have apparently maintained a cohesive partnership.

"[The week] was a little different, but I just think the biggest thing we took from all this is that we're all in this together," Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark told Albert Breer of The MMQB. "C.P. and Pett, they have a great relationship and we all have a great relationship with those guys, too. So, I think that's just sticking together and understanding that. That's huge for us."

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer felt compelled to act as Dallas continued to have one of the NFL's worst defenses. Taking the play sheet away from Parker while keeping him on the staff risked creating a very difficult situation.

Parker was candid when he said he weighed stepping down altogether.

It's too early to say whether the change has made a positive impact. The Cowboys won in Week 11 but allowed 346 yards and 30 points to a Tennessee Titans offense that has been inconsistent at best.

Maybe Schottenheimer was justified in shuffling the defensive duties around. The results were terrible, and the 34-year-old Parker may not have been ready for a coordinator role, especially with such a high-profile team.

Parker is nonetheless in a tough spot by sticking around.

If the defense does start to show sustained improvement, the credit will likely go to Pettine rather than the guy who's officially the defensive coordinator. Regardless of what happens the rest of the season, Parker could be a lame duck.

articles.title: The real reason Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce started the New Heights podcast will move you
articles.summary: For Travis and Jason Kelce, New Heights was never just about football.
articles.body: For Travis and Jason Kelce, New Heights was never just about football. Long before the podcast became a major hit and brought the brothers closer to millions of fans, it had a much more personal beginning. Travis simply missed spending time with his older brother.The two Kelce brothers spent years building their NFL careers, often on opposite sides of the country and dealing with the demands of professional football. While they always shared a close relationship, their busy schedules did not necessarily leave them with enough time to catch up like ordinary brothers.That was something Travis wanted to change.Travis Kelce had a surprisingly personal reason for starting New HeightsIn a throwback confession about the podcast's beginnings, Travis explained that he and Jason wanted to create something that would give them dedicated time together every week."To be honest, me and Jason just missed each other. Now we have two hours set aside every single week to talk football, catch up on things, and just be brothers," Travis said.It was a simple reason, but one that made the idea behind New Heights even more special. Rather than looking at it as another business opportunity, Travis saw the podcast as a chance to reconnect with his brother and make their conversations a regular part of their lives. And as fans would eventually discover, those conversations were worth listening to.Travis and Jason were never as different as people thoughtAnother interesting part of Travis' confession was how he described the contrasting personalities of the two brothers. According to Travis, people often viewed him and Jason as being on completely different sides of the spectrum. Their fashion choices alone were enough to create that impression.Travis likes to dress up and keep his appearance fresh, while Jason has become famous for his relaxed approach to fashion. Travis even joked about his brother wearing flip-flops in the snow, describing him as almost a Neanderthal when it comes to that side of life.But according to Travis, people did not always recognise how much the brothers actually had in common until they were sitting together in the same room.He wanted New Heights to give people a closer look at that connection.New Heights became a way for fans to see their brotherhoodWhat started as two brothers wanting to spend more time together eventually turned into something much bigger.The podcast gave fans an opportunity to see a different side of Travis and Jason, beyond their performances on the football field. Their playful arguments, jokes, stories about growing up and occasional disagreements became a major part of the show's appeal.It also showed how comfortable the brothers were around each other. Jason could tease Travis, Travis could make fun of Jason's fashion choices, and neither seemed particularly interested in holding back.That natural chemistry helped make New Heights stand out.For fans, the podcast became more than another place to hear NFL discussions. It offered a glimpse into the relationship between two brothers who had spent years competing at the highest level of professional football.And perhaps that is what makes Travis' old confession so memorable.The brothers did not need a complicated business plan or a grand idea to start talking every week. They just needed a reason to make time for each other.Sometimes, the best things really do begin with something as simple as missing your brother.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mr. Irrelevant - Official 'Who Is John Tuggle' Featurette - IGN
articles.summary:
Join star David Corenswet for a behind-the-scenes look at Mr. Irrelevant in this video for the upcoming film starring David Corenswet, Isabel May, David Krumholtz, Tuwaine Barrett, Thaddeus LaGrone, Alexander England, Spencer House, Tandi Wright, and Michael Shannon.Mr. Irrelevant is the inspiring true story of John Tuggle (David Corenswet), the last player selected in the last round of the 1983 NFL draft by the New York Giants. A true underdog, Tuggle defied expectations on the field and off for his then first-year head coach, Bill Parcells (Michael Shannon), his newfound love (Isabel May), and his team, proving that remarkable hope and perseverance can transcend even the greatest challenges.

Mr. Irrelevant is produced by David Ellison, Dana Goldberg, Don Granger, Jonathan Levine, Gillian Bohrer, and Nick Santora. Jesse Sisgold, Jason T. Reed, Sandino Moya-Smith, Stan Wlodkowski, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Ross Ketover, Ken Rodgers, and Jessica Boddy serve as executive producers. It is written by Nick Santora. Mr. Irrelevant, directed by Jonathan Levine, opens in theaters on December 25, 2026.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk Released by 49ers, NFL Rumors Link Jayden Daniels' Commanders as Possible Landing Spot
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are releasing wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, officially ending his tumultuous ending in town, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are releasing wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, officially ending his tumultuous ending in town, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported a practice squad contract with the Washington Commanders is viewed as "the most likely option."

Aiyuk starred with the Sun Devils starred at Arizona State before the San Francisco 49ers selected him as the No. 25 choice in the 2020 NFL draft. He enjoyed two 1,000-yard seasons in 2022 and 2023, catching 78 passes for 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns in the first year before adding a 75/1,342/7 stat line during the 49ers' NFC-winning 2023 season.

Unfortunately, Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus on Oct. 20, 2024 during a game against the Kansas City Chiefs. he missed all of 2024 and then 2025 as his situation with the team became murkier. David Bonilla of 49ers Webzone provided more details.

"San Francisco initially expected Aiyuk to return sometime during the 2025 season, but that never materialized. Questions also arose during his recovery, as the receiver reportedly did not participate in team-directed rehabilitation or meetings. Aiyuk's communication with the organization eventually ceased, prompting the 49ers to place him on the reserve/left squad list, officially ending his season."

In Nov. 2025 , 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters that the team voided his guaranteed money ($26.15 million, per The Athletic ) for the 2026 season.

At the beginning of training camp, 49ers general manager John Lynch all but said Aiyuk's time with the team was over.

"Brandon is on a left squad designation," Lynch told reporters . "As such, he's not on our 90-man roster. I, personally, and we as an organization, are going to focus on the players that are here. I don't have anything to add to that. We wish him well. We wish his family well."

If there was an small opening that Aiyuk could ever return that closed this summer as took numerous shots at Shanahan and Lynch.

The 49ers' insistence that Aiyuk wouldn't play for the team again continued into this season, even as he applied for his reinstatement in early November and met with the team.

If Aiyuk winds up with the Commanders, he'll reunite with his former Arizona State teammate and close friend, quarterback Jayden Daniels. It's a great opportunity for Aiyuk to get back on track and perhaps return closer to the form shown in 2022 and 2023.

Reports had connected Aiyuk to the Commanders. ESPN's John Keim provided one back on March 19.

"One intriguing name could be San Francisco 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk. Multiple team sources said Washington is well aware of Aiyuk's desire to play with Daniels. But Aiyuk remains under contract and the Commanders would be unlikely to trade for him or, when free, sign him to anything other than a one-year, prove-it deal."

The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala reported on Sunday that Aiyuk and Daniels are "now on good terms" again after the receiver previously called out the quarterback on social media.

articles.title: New Brandon Aiyuk Rumors Reveal NFL Teams' Concerns About Former 49ers WR Amid Landing Spot Buzz
articles.summary: After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers following months of tension, wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk reportedly may have a complicated market.
articles.body:
After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers following months of tension, wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk reportedly may have a complicated market.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported, "Some teams I've spoken [to] are skeptical [that] Brandon Aiyuk will walk right into a job. At least three unknown variables exist: Health, conditioning, motivation."

Still, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noted that the Washington Commanders' practice squad is "viewed as the most likely option" for Aiyuk.

ESPN's Nick Wagoner explained that Aiyuk will be subjected to waivers since his release came after this month's trade deadline. If he goes unclaimed in the next 24 hours, he will become an unrestricted free agent.

Wagoner added that the dead money remaining on Aiyuk's deal will be split into $12.35 million for 2026 and $19.29 million in 2027, but the 49ers "will receive a cap credit of nearly $5 million in March and are also aiming to recoup additional bonus money from Aiyuk."

49ers general manager John Lynch said in January that Aiyuk's time with the franchise was over after he sat out the entire 2025 season while recovering from a knee injury. The saga finally reached a resolution when Aiyuk applied for reinstatement with the NFL and reported to the team earlier this month.

Aiyuk has been linked to the Commanders for quite some time due to his previous relationship with star quarterback Jayden Daniels dating back to their days together at Arizona State. Washington lost star receiver Terry McLaurin to season-ending knee surgery, so the team could use another reliable pass-catcher in the mix.

As Fowler noted, "buying low isn't the worst thing" for a team pursuing Aiyuk. The 28-year-old could still be effective in the right situation, so it could be worth it to give him a look on the practice squad.

articles.title: Cardinals DC Nick Rallis Fired Amid 3-8 Record, New NFL Rumors Reveal Interim DC
articles.summary: Changes are coming in Arizona.
articles.body:
The Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter , with senior defensive assistant coach Teryl Austin now "expected" to handle interim defensive coordinator duties.

The move doesn't come as a huge surprise.

The Cardinals have given up 30 or more points in four of their last five games and eight times overall in 11 games. They are just 3-8 overall.

In parts of four seasons leading the defense Rallis has never had a unit finish better than 21st in yards allowed, while the defense has been 29th or worse in points allowed three times, including this season.

Rallis was originally hired by former head coach Jonathan Gannon in 2023 after the pair worked together with the Philadelphia Eagles, and first-year head coach Mike LaFleur chose to keep him aboard when he took the job. That partnership ended after 11 games, however.

The Cardinals remain a franchise in disarray and are headed for a fifth straight losing season, barring an unfathomably unlikely turnaround. Coming into the 2026 campaign, Arizona had one playoff appearance in the past 10 seasons.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker, Emmett Johnson's Roles Updated by Eric Bieniemy, Fantasy Outlook for Chiefs RBs
articles.summary: While Emmet Johnson has excelled in Kenneth Walker III's absence, he'll remain the No. 2 running back for the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body:
While Emmet Johnson has excelled in Kenneth Walker III's absence, he'll remain the No. 2 running back for the Kansas City Chiefs.

Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy updated the two running backs' roles on Monday, saying Walker would start if he's healthy.

"Kenneth is the starter," he told reporters . "If Kenneth is to play, he'll remain the starter... We're coaching that next man to be prepared to be the man. Emmett has done a great job, but we also understand the value that Kenneth brings as well."

Walker was sidelined for Week 10's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons because of a groin injury and missed Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals as well, though head coach Andy Reid indicated that holding him out in Week 11 was mostly a precautionary measure.

Reid told reporters that the team didn't want to do "something stupid" and felt it was wise to wait until Walker was "feeling better."

Walker being out gave Johnson the chance to show what he can do. The rookie rushed for 101 yards on 22 carries against the Falcons, adding 70 yards through the air and two touchdowns. Against the Cardinals, he had 105 rushing yards, 38 receiving yards and a touchdown. He had previously never recorded more than 34 rushing yards in a game.

Those familiar with Johnson likely aren't too surprised by his recent breakout. Last year at Nebraska, he rushed for 1,451 yards and 12 touchdowns.

While fantasy managers who rostered Johnson might be reeling after his two monster games, it might be time to temper expectations. He surely earned a bigger role in the offense, but as Bieniemy said, he'll be the backup once again when Walker returns.

Despite missing two games, Walker still has the fifth-most rushing yards this season (872), to go along with seven touchdowns on the ground and four through the air.

His status for Thursday's game against the Buffalo Bills is still up in the air, but he'll look to return to form if he's able to play.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni Addresses Potential Daniel Jones Pursuit After Joe Milton Helps Eagles Beat Steelers

"Won't get too much into that," he said. "We are happy with our room and who we have and who we're working with. Coming off of Joe playing well yesterday, that hasn't been in our discussions."

The Eagles are coming off a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday behind Joe Milton, but with Jalen Hurts out for the season, it's been speculated that the Eagles could look for more help at the quarterback position.

"We like that room," Sirriani said. "We feel like Tanner (McKee) is very capable to go out there and lead the team. Joe, obviously coming off of his best performance, and then to develop, working with Cole (Payton) and developing there, (we) feel good about that room. But won't get too much more into that, though."

articles.title: DK Metcalf Not Suspended for DeJean Altercation on Video During Steelers-Eagles, NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf won't be suspended following his ejection from Sunday's contest against the Philadelphia Eagles, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf won't be suspended following his ejection from Sunday's contest against the Philadelphia Eagles, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Metcalf was ejected from the contest against the Eagles in the third quarter after receiving his second unsportsmanlike penalty of the game.

The first penalty on Metcalf came in the second quarter after an altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean. In the third, he was jawing with safety Marcus Epps before a scrum broke out. Metcalf appeared to reach into DeJean's helmet, and DeJean then seemed to complain about having his eye poked.

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said after the game that he was told by an official that Metcalf poked an Eagles player in the eye, thus resulting in the unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

DeJean clarified after the game that Metcalf "almost" poked him in the eye.

Pittsburgh went on to lose the game 19-16.

"This was definitely a game we expected to win. I think his particular case performance-wise, I think our process, I think our men do a good job of looking in the mirror. And you know, we've got a short week," McCarthy told reporters after the game. "We'll sit down and address everything.

"Especially, we need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to get thrown out of the game. He's one of the 48. It's about everything we do through the week is to put those guys in position to be successful."

Metcalf—who left the locker room on Sunday without speaking to reporters—addressed the situation on Monday:

The ejection was Metcalf's third of his career, and he's tied with Dre Greenlaw for the most ejections since he was drafted in 2019. Last season, Metcalf was suspended for two games because of an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan.

Metcalf has had a frustrating season, recording just 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns in 10 games.

articles.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf reportedly won't be suspended, denies he tried to poke Eagles' Cooper DeJean in the eye
articles.summary: "You said I tried to what?" Metcalf responded when asked about the alleged eye poke.
articles.body:
DK Metcalf says he didn't try to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

He also won't be serving a suspension. Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, the NFL won't suspend the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver following his ejection from Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . Per the report, Metcalf could still be subject to a fine.

Metcalf was ejected due to two personal fouls, both related to scuffles with DeJean, a cornerback for the Eagles. Per Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, a referee told him that Metcalf "poked a defender in the eye."

Metcalf didn't speak with media after the 19-16 loss . He was available at his locker on Monday and confirmed to reporters that "I was avoiding y'all" on Sunday. This was prior to the report that he won't be suspended.

Here's Metcalf's response when asked about "when you tried to poke Cooper in the eye."

"You said I tried to what?" Metcalf responded. "I didn't try to poke him in the eye. … I was just telling him to stop pushing me. That's all I said."

Here's video of the altercation that led to Metcalf's second personal foul penalty and ejection. The video shows Metcalf with his right hand pushing at DeJean's facemask. It's taken from a distance and blurry.

Metcalf's first personal foul was for this scuffle, also involving DeJean.

Not seen in the above clip, Metcalf also grabbed the facemask of Eagles safety Andrew Mukuba and shoved his head back. He also swiped at the arm of an official when the official put his hand on his chest to try to separate Metcalf from the scrum.

As for the alleged eye poke, DeJean told reporters after the game that Metcalf "just missed" poking him in the eye.

"Almost, almost," DeJean said when asked if he got poked in the eye. "He just missed. … We were just competing. Things like that happen in football. "It wasn't anything crazy. Nobody was really saying anything, two guys were going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me. Things like that. Obviously it carried over to whatever that was at the end."

"Almost, almost," DeJean said when asked if he got poked in the eye. "He just missed. … We were just competing. Things like that happen in football.

"It wasn't anything crazy. Nobody was really saying anything, two guys were going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me. Things like that. Obviously it carried over to whatever that was at the end."

On Monday, Metcalf declined to offer details of his side of the altercations beyond denying that he tried to poke DeJean in the eye.

"Can't remember," he responded when asked what happened between him and DeJean. "You've gotta ask him."

This is not the first time Metcalf has been accused of poking or trying to poke an opponent in the eye.

During a Week 8 game in 2025, Walker was penalized and later fined $12,172 for this incident in which he stuck a finger inside the facemask of Packers linebacker Quay Walker.

It's not clear as of Monday if Metcalf will receive further discipline from the NFL for Sunday's incidents against the Eagles.

Metcalf is in his second season with the Steelers after six seasons with the Seahawks that featured two Pro Bowl selections. His first season in Pittsburgh produced the lowest output of his career, 59 catches for 850 yards and 6 touchdowns.

Through 10 games this season, Metcalf is on pace to fall short of those season-long numbers with 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns. He had one catch for two yards at the time of his ejection Sunday late in the third quarter.

NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS Metcalf was ejected from the Eagles game because NFL rules stipulate any player flagged twice for unsportsmanlike conduct related to taunting, abusive conduct or striking another player, is automatically disqualified. But that was around 2020-2023 with the Seattle Seahawks. The numbers – yards, receptions, touchdowns – have been in steady decline since 2024, including the past two seasons with the Steelers. articles.title: Ravens' Potential Daniel Jones Pursuit Addressed by HC After Colts Trade Rumors at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens reportedly made an offer to acquire quarterback Daniel Jones from the Indianapolis Colts ahead of the NFL trade deadline. That deal never materialized, and Baltimore's interest may have faded away.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens reportedly made an offer to acquire quarterback Daniel Jones from the Indianapolis Colts ahead of the NFL trade deadline. That deal never materialized, and Baltimore's interest may have faded away.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter was asked on Monday if the team might pursue Jones now that he is a free agent.

"I'm OK with the quarterback room and I'm not going to speculate on other players," Minter said, according to Jonas Shaffer of The Baltimore Banner.

Baltimore was searching for a stopgap option at the position after star quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a season-ending injury earlier this month. The Ravens ultimately sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Arizona Cardinals in exchange for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Baltimore is only responsible for Brissett's $2.43 million base salary since the Cardinals restructured his contract before the trade to absorb most of the salary cap hit, according to ESPN . Still, adding another quarterback would take additional cap space — and there's no guarantee that Jones would even provide an upgrade over Brissett.

Jones was released a day after Indianapolis suffered a 26-3 loss against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. The Colts benched the 29-year-old late in the fourth quarter of that loss after he completed just 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with zero touchdowns and one interception.

In his 11 starts this season, Jones mustered just 1,974 passing yards with seven touchdowns and a league-high 13 interceptions. He has also had his worst season as a runner with a career-low 8.9 rushing yards per game.

The Ravens suffered a narrow 35-33 defeat against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. They have now lost six consecutive games since winning four of their first five contests to start to the season.

articles.title: Marlon Humphrey Returns to Ravens After Comments About Baltimore, CB Was Inactive for Panthers Loss

articles.title: Top NFL Landing Spots for Brandon Aiyuk After 49ers Finally Release WR
articles.summary: The ongoing stare-down between wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk and the San Francisco 49ers has come to an end. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported early Monday afternoon that the 49ers will release the 28-year-old pass-catcher.
articles.body:
The ongoing stare-down between wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk and the San Francisco 49ers has come to an end. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported early Monday afternoon that the 49ers will release the 28-year-old pass-catcher.

Aiyuk's release comes after the NFL granted his reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list on November 9. San Francisco was given a two-week roster exemption upon his reinstatement, and with that coming to an end, the 49ers apparently decided it was time to officially part ways.

Since Aiyuk's release comes after the trade deadline, he will be subject to waivers. If he goes unclaimed by Tuesday afternoon, he'll be free to sign with any team.

Here, you'll find a look at six NFL teams that would make perfect sense for Aiyuk in 2026 based on factors like scheme fit, coaching familiarity, potential opportunity, and roster needs. First, though, let's examine what Aiyuk has to offer receiver-needy teams for the final stretch of the regular season.

To be clear, Aiyuk won't automatically be a target for every receiver-needy team. The 49ers released him because of a significant rift that was reportedly first opened last year when Aiyuk stopped showing up for treatment for the knee injury he suffered the previous season.

The divide has only grown since then, with Aiyuk verbally disparaging the 49ers on social media, and the franchise showing no interest in bringing him back onto the field.

There's a lot for teams to unpack there, and not every team will be comfortable with his health, work ethic, team commitment, and public personality—at least, not without bringing him in for a closer look first.

That said, teams that are comfortable with Aiyuk the person could greatly benefit by adding Aiyuk the player, provided he is 100 percent healthy.

On the field, Aiyuk has been a tremendous route-runner with enough breakaway speed and contested-catch ability to serve in a No. 1 role. The 6'0", 200-pound Arizona State product can play on the perimeter or in the slot and has shown he can handle a high-volume role.

In 2023, Aiyuk racked up 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on 75 receptions.

Any team claiming Aiyuk would only owe a prorated portion of his $1.2 million 2026 base salary. That would make him a bargain for cap-tight contenders that need help for the playoff push.

Aiyuk could also appeal to rebuilding teams that could audition him for a long-term role. Aiyuk won't turn 29 until March and could be a high-level contributor for several more seasons.

Will Aiyuk make an immediate impact after roughly two years away from the playing field? Probably not, but he could potentially be back in pre-injury form by the final month of the regular season.

The Las Vegas Raiders probably won't be pushing for the postseason over the final month of the season. They've lost seven of their last eight, and they're rapidly falling behind in the AFC's wild-card race.

However, the rest of the season is all about developing quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza . Adding Aiyuk could help with that process and could potentially help Mendoza well beyond the current season.

Las Vegas already has strong support pieces in running back offensive tackle Kolton Miller, tight end Brock Bowers, center Tyler Linderbaum, and running back Ashton Jeanty. Tre Tucker has also flashed at times, and Mendoza seems to have a growing rapport with wideout Jack Bech.

Still, the Raiders could use help on the perimeter, and Aiyuk would be a terrific fit for their offense. Head coach Klint Kubiak was San Francisco's passing game coordinator during Aiyuk's career campaign in 2023.

The Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 season as presumptive Super Bowl favorites. However, they've stumbled often en route to a 6-4 record, and they now have a massive need at receiver.

Los Angeles had one of the league's top receiver duos in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. However, Adams is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, while Nacua recently underwent knee surgery that is expected to end his season. Additionally, the Rams have lost tight end Tarrance Ferguson to a season-ending ankle injury.

If the Rams are going to make any sort of significant playoff push, Matthew Stafford needs to establish new go-to targets.

Aiyuk would be a sensible addition for the Rams, even if he wouldn't be a major asset until closer to the postseason. His route-running, body control, and after-the-catch ability aren't wholly unlike those of Nacua, even if there's a clear gap in both talent and upside.

L.A. could also provide Aiyuk with a strong schematic fit, as Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay run extremely similar offenses. Rams GM Les Snead has never been shy about taking big swings at talented players, and he made a similar move roughly five years ago by adding Odell Beckham Jr. following his November release.

Less than a year ago, the New England Patriots were playing in Super Bowl LX. Now, they're more akin to the Raiders than playoff hopefuls like the Rams.

New England currently sits at .500 but may have lost quarterback Drake Maye for the season. The third-year signal-caller has a fractured fibula and could miss most or all of the remaining schedule, according to Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN.

However, auditioning Aiyuk for the future would make plenty of sense for the Patriots. Maye is a young quarterback who needs a better crop of receivers around him. Top executive Eliot Wolf tried to improve the situation by trading for A.J. Brown in the offseason, but Brown has largely disappointed.

Aiyuk probably wouldn't get to work with Maye this season, but the Patriots could get a look at how Aiyuk can operate in Josh McDaniels' offense by adding him now.

And New England has had interest in Aiyuk before. Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reported back in 2024 that the Patriots and 49ers had the framework of a trade in place before San Francisco pivoted and extended Aiyuk instead.

The Patriots aren't the only receiver-needy team that previously had interest in Aiyuk. According to Maiocco , the Pittsburgh Steelers wanted Aiyuk in 2024 but ultimately "declined to meet the 49ers' trade demands."

The Steelers are a different team now, with a different quarterback and coach in Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy. However, GM Omar Khan is still running the show, and Pittsburgh still has a need at receiver.

Injuries have created a revolving door opposite DK Metcalf, and it's not as if Metcalf has been a stellar No. 1 target. The 28-year-old has provided a passer rating of only 70.4 when targeted this season.

Pittsburgh is very much in the playoff hunt at 6-4. However, the Steelers have lost two straight and desperately need to bolster their 24th-ranked passing attack. It's worth taking a flier on Aiyuk, even if he only provides a minor boost during the regular season.

The Rams aren't the only NFC West team that could (and should) have interest in taking Aiyuk off of San Francisco's hands.

The Seattle Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions but have had their own run of bad injury luck and sit at 6-4. They still have a legitimate shot at repeating, though, because they have a championship-caliber defense and a top-flight receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Despite Seattle's flip-flopping between quarterbacks Sam Darnold and Drew Lock because of injuries, Smith-Njigba leads the league with a whopping 1,207 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He's on pace to set a new single-season receiving record and has accounted for over half of the Seahawks' receiving yards this year.

Unfortunately, the Seahawks lack reliable depth behind Smith-Njigba. Cooper Kupp is the team's No. 2 receiver with just 272 yards. It's worth seeing if Ayiuk can boost the overall group, as he'd be a natural fit for the offense. Coordinator Brian Fleury spent seven seasons on San Francisco's staff before joining Seattle in 2025.

The Washington Commanders have rarely looked like contenders in 2026, but they're still alive in the NFC East race. They could also use receiving help, both this season and beyond.

Washington has already lost top receiver Terry McLaurin to a season-ending ACL tear, and he'll turn 32 early next season. Stefon Diggs has been a fine fill-in this season, but he's probably not going to be a multi-year target for quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Aiyuk, who played with Daniels for a season at Arizona State, could be. He also publicly criticized his former quarterback on social media, but he and Daniels are back on good terms, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler :

"Sources told ESPN that after talking things out, Daniels was receptive and understanding of Aiyuk."

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport recently called Washington Aiyuk's "most likely landing spot." It will be interesting to see if any other teams make a run at him via waivers in an effort to keep him away from the Commanders.

articles.title: Daniel Jones Becomes FA After Clearing Waivers Amid NFL Rumors on Patriots, Potential Landing Spots
articles.summary: After being released by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday, Daniel Jones is now cleared to join a new team.
articles.body:
After being released by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday, Daniel Jones is now cleared to join a new team.

Per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the veteran quarterback cleared waivers on Monday and is officially a free agent. The New England Patriots, who are expected to be without quarterback Drake Maye for most, if not the rest, of the regular season, aren't interested in Jones, according to NFL insider Josina Anderson.

Along with the Patriots, a handful of teams could use a quarterback to finish out the regular season. The Philadelphia Eagles, who lost Jalen Hurts for the season due to blood clots, are one, but they also aren't planning to pursue him, head coach Nick Sirianni said Monday.

"Won't get too much into that," he said, per The Athletic's Brooks Kubena . "We are happy with our room and who we have and who we're working with. Coming off of Joe playing well yesterday, that hasn't been in our discussions."

The Baltimore Ravens attempted to trade for Jones at the deadline, but head coach Jesse Minter said they won't turn to him in free agency amid Lamar Jackson's thumb injury.

"I'm OK with the quarterback room and I'm not going to speculate on other players," Minter said, according to Jonas Shaffer of The Baltimore Banner.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic noted, following Jones' release, that the Arizona Cardinals could be a potential landing spot, but it remains to be seen whether they'll pursue him or stick with Gardner Minshew under center.

While Jones might be an upgrade at quarterback for a handful of teams, his contract is also pretty steep. He has $2.35 million remaining this year, with $2.1 million of that guaranteed. He's also owed $38 million in non-guaranteed money next year.

To pay that much for Jones, a team would have to be confident that he could help them compete for a championship. After the way he started the season, few teams likely have that kind of confidence.

Jones had a breakout season in 2025 before tearing his Achilles late in the year. This season, he's thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions.

At this point, it could be best for Jones to wait to hit free agency this offseason and hit the reset button with a new team.

articles.title: 49ers release veteran WR Brandon Aiyuk, who must pass through waivers before becoming a free agent
articles.summary: Aiyuk will become a free agent if he clears waivers.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have released veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. He must clear waivers, and teams have until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday to claim him.

This ends the months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

Aiyuk is subject to waivers, but if he clears them, he will be a free agent. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that a spot on the Washington Commanders' practice squad is the likeliest next step for the veteran wide receiver.

After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on Nov. 9, at which time the 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption to decide if they wanted to release him, trade him or add him to the 53-man roster. The reinstatement was the first step toward Aiyuk's eventual release.

Aiyuk's breakup with the Niners is no surprise. Leading up to the 2025 season, reports surfaced that guarantees in his contract were voided amid growing frustrations between the organization and the veteran wideout.

Then, in January, 49ers GM John Lynch officially acknowledged the impending divorce between the two sides, stating in his end-of-season news conference, "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers."

Aiyuk is 28 and hasn't played since Week 7 of the 2024 season. Before his injury, he had spent his entire five-year career with the 49ers.

San Francisco drafted him with the 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He had his breakout season in 2022, finishing with 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns. Aiyuk returned in 2023 and improved, finishing with 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

He suffered his injury in 2024 against the Kansas City Chiefs. This kicked off two years of wide receiver injuries for the 49ers.

San Francisco has been playing this season without Aiyuk in consideration for the roster. As such, the Niners have turned to Deebo Samuel, Mike Evans and Keenan Allen in the passing game, with promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling expected to return from injury soon.

If Aiyuk joins Washington, the Commanders will look to get him up to speed as No. 1 wide receiver Terry McLaurin has been ruled out for the season due to a torn ACL. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams have picked up the slack, but Washington could use Aiyuk if he can play close to his pre-injury level.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Star's Return Timeline Ahead of Packers vs. Rams
articles.summary: Micah Parsons is back.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers star edge rusher, sidelined since Dec. 14 of last year with a torn ACL and meniscus, has been cleared to play and is set to make his season debut against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday.

The report comes shortly after Parsons told reporters that he was still awaiting clearance from his doctor to play.

"I really don't know yet," he said Monday. "I still gotta talk to (Dr. Neal) ElAttrache, I still gotta get cleared from my surgical doctor, so we'll see."

He said he had to have a conference call with his doctor, in which they'd go over testing and other metrics to make sure he's "100 percent ready."

"I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said last week that the team planned for Parsons to be available for Wednesday's game against the Rams, though he clarified that Parsons still had a "couple more hurdles to clear."

Parsons seemingly cleared those hurdles and is now set to return to action for the first time in nearly a year.

In his last fully healthy season in 2023, Parsons was tremendous, recording 64 tackles and 14 sacks as a member of the Dallas Cowboys. While he missed the last three games of the season last year, he still recorded 41 tackles and 12.5 sacks.

He has some rust to shake off, but will look to return to that form this year.

Parsons' return comes amid a 6-4 start to the year for the Packers, who are hoping to finish the year strong and make a deep playoff run. Green Bay currently sits in last place in the loaded NFC North but is still in playoff position.

But a win over the Rams this week could go a long way, as Los Angeles is also 6-4 and looking to move ahead of the Packers in the standings.

Picking up a win against the Rams gets much easier with Parsons now back in the fold.

articles.title: Travis Kelce drops four-word hint about retirement after breaking Rob Gronkowski's NFL record
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is giving Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to believe his NFL career is far from over.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is giving Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to believe his NFL career is far from over. At 37, the veteran tight end continues to deliver when his team needs him most. While questions about retirement have followed him throughout the season, his latest performance against the Arizona Cardinals offered a compelling response. Kelce reached another historic milestone during Kansas City's 34-7 victory, moving past Rob Gronkowski on the NFL's all-time tight end touchdown list. However, it was his brief postgame remark that caught even more attention.Travis Kelce overtakes Rob Gronkowski as Chiefs star closes in on NFL historyKelce made his presence felt early against Arizona, finding the end zone twice before halftime. Those scores took his career touchdown tally to 110, including playoff appearances, putting him ahead of Gronkowski's 108. He now has two legendary tight ends within reach.Tony Gonzalez holds the next position with 115 touchdowns, while Antonio Gates leads the list with 118. With five more scores, Kelce could draw level with Gonzalez. Eight additional touchdowns would put him alongside Gates.The achievement becomes even more impressive when his age is considered. Kelce also joined an exclusive group of players who have recorded multiple touchdowns in one half at 37 or older. The group includes Jim Thorpe, Steve Young and Jerry Rice.Reacting to the company he has joined, Kelce said, “That’s good company right there. That’s an iconic group.”His performance also strengthened his case as Kansas City's leading receiving option. He finished the Cardinals game with six catches for 74 yards, taking his 2026 season totals to 41 receptions, 586 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns, along with one rushing score.Patrick Mahomes backs Travis Kelce as retirement speculation continuesThe biggest talking point, however, came after the final whistle. When asked about playing his 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead Stadium, Kelce responded with four words: “Cheers to 100 more.”Although the comment could have been a lighthearted celebration, it offered an encouraging glimpse into his current mindset. Kelce has not announced any retirement plans, and his performance suggests he still has plenty to offer.Patrick Mahomes also praised his teammate's commitment, particularly his willingness to keep practising despite dealing with an ankle injury.“You can’t take that dude off the football field. He loves it. He’s a Hall of Famer, and he’s the one that wants to get in there every single rep, that kind of gives you the mindset to tell the other guys, ‘Hey, y’all want to take a rep off? Look at this guy.’ It’s just easy for me as a leader to have someone like that on my team.”With Kansas City sitting at 8-2, another deep playoff run could give Kelce even more motivation. His current deal covers the 2026 season, leaving a possible return in 2027 open. For now, his focus remains on winning, while the chase for Gonzalez and Gates gives him two more historic targets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
