articles.title: “I am very proud that through the work..” : How Travis Kelce's $20,000 charity effort in Missouri gave schoolchildren a new gym floor and showed his commitment and love for Kansas City
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has given Kansas City plenty of reasons to cheer for him on the football field.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has given Kansas City plenty of reasons to cheer for him on the football field. However, one of his memorable moments away from the NFL came in May 2017, when the Kansas City Chiefs tight end teamed up with UnitedHealthcare to support students in Oak Grove, Missouri. Their $20,000 contribution helped Maple Elementary School get a new gym floor and supported the district's food programme.The visit was about more than a donation for Kelce. He spent time with the children, played games on the new floor and spoke about his connection with Kansas City. The tight end also explained how his foundation helped make the school project possible, giving students a better place to stay active and enjoy their time together.Travis Kelce's $20,000 donation gave Oak Grove students a new gym floorOn May 9, 2017, Kelce visited Maple Elementary School in Oak Grove for the dedication of its new gym floor. The Chiefs tight end partnered with UnitedHealthcare through his charitable work to help fund the project.According to FOX 4 Kansas City, UnitedHealthcare contributed $15,000 to Kelce's Dreambuilders programme for the gym project. The company also donated another $5,000 to the Oak Grove School District's food programme. The Kansas City Chiefs later reported the $20,000 contribution as support for the district through the partnership.Kelce expressed his happiness about making the project possible in a statement carried by Arrowhead Addict in its May 10, 2017 report."I am very proud that through the work I do with my foundation, Eighty-Seven & Running, I was able to partner with UnitedHealthcare in making sure this important repair was possible," Kelce said.He also explained why the new floor meant so much to the school."A safe, new floor was really important to Maple Elementary, and I’m thrilled that the students can stay active and have fun playing together as a team."The children made the occasion even more special when Kelce walked into the gym. Around 500 young Chiefs supporters welcomed him with cheers. Speaking to FOX 4 Kansas City during the May 9 dedication, he shared how much the city meant to him."I really love Kansas City. It’s home for me now. I’ve embraced the city just like they’ve embraced me," Kelce said.He also explained what he wanted to achieve through his community work."I want to make sure that I can get out here to the community just as much as they get to a Chiefs game. And not only that but make sure I make a difference."UnitedHealthcare also explained why it chose Oak Grove for the contribution. Michael Margherio, the company's vice president of sales, told FOX 4 Kansas City at the event:"We picked Oak Grove Schools because they have been a client of ours for over ten years. They are really the model for helping their employees lead healthier lives so it worked out wonderful for us today."Kelce did not leave after the dedication. He played games with the students on their new gym floor, signed autographs and took pictures with them.How Travis Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation supported children beyond footballThe Oak Grove visit was part of Kelce's larger commitment to helping young people. He established his Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation in 2015 to support underserved children through education, mentoring, athletics and other opportunities.His own childhood played a role in that decision. Growing up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, Kelce understood that some children lacked access to the opportunities and resources they needed. He wanted to use his position as an NFL player to help young people pursue their ambitions.The May 2017 donation also came during a strong period in his football career. Kelce had signed a five-year, $46.8 million contract extension with Kansas City in January 2016. He followed it with an impressive 2016 season, recording 85 receptions for 1,125 receiving yards and four touchdowns. He also earned first-team All-Pro honours.His community work continued that same week. On May 12, 2017, the Chiefs reported that Kelce and fellow tight ends had surprised fifth-grade students from Immanuel Lutheran School at Arrowhead Stadium. The children enjoyed a stadium tour and a Play 60 football clinic.For the Maple Elementary students, the new gym floor meant a safer place to play and stay active. For Kelce, the visit offered a chance to give something back to a city that had welcomed him with open arms. articles.title: Why did the Cleveland Browns reject Daniel Jones? Shedeur Sanders retains No. 2 QB spot as Cleveland rules out signing former Colts quarterback
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have reportedly ruled out a move for Daniel Jones after the Indianapolis Colts released the quarterback.
articles.body: The Cleveland Browns have reportedly ruled out a move for Daniel Jones after the Indianapolis Colts released the quarterback. Despite questions about their quarterback depth, Cleveland has no interest in bringing him in, according to a new report. The decision also offers some clarity about Shedeur Sanders, who continues to hold the No. 2 spot behind Deshaun Watson despite competition from Dillon Gabriel.Jones cleared waivers on November 23, 2026, which opened the door for interested teams to approach him. However, the Browns do not appear ready to add another quarterback. Instead, they are sticking with their current group, keeping Sanders in line for another opportunity if Watson cannot play.Browns have no interest in bringing Daniel Jones to ClevelandBrowns reporter Mary Kay Cabot confirmed the team's position in a post on X. She wrote, "The #Browns have no interest in signing QB Daniel Jones, who cleared waivers today after being released by the #Colts."The decision comes with Cleveland already carrying four other quarterbacks alongside its current options. Deshaun Watson leads the group, with Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green also on the roster. Adding Jones would have created another layer of competition, particularly for the young quarterbacks looking to establish themselves.Watson, meanwhile, won the starting job ahead of Sanders after returning from a recurring right Achilles injury. His return in 2026 has helped Cleveland put together a 6-4 record.Through nine starts this season, Watson has completed 188 of 289 passes for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. His 65.1% completion rate has given the Browns a reliable option under center, although a recent injury scare forced the coaching staff to look elsewhere.During Cleveland's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter. He initially cleared the evaluation and returned to action. However, he later experienced concussion symptoms and entered the league's concussion protocol. That opened the door for Sanders.Shedeur Sanders remains Deshaun Watson's backup after strong Saints showingSanders started against the New Orleans Saints and delivered one of his better performances. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns. However, Cleveland suffered a narrow 23-22 defeat.Despite the loss, head coach Todd Monken liked what he saw from the rookie quarterback. Speaking after the Saints game, Monken praised Sanders' preparation and composure while acknowledging that he still had areas to improve."I'm awfully proud of Shedeur," Monken said. "It had been 10 weeks since he really had reps with the starters in practice. I was hopeful he would play because he had a great week of practice."I thought he battled and showed composure in the pocket. He made some plays with his feet. The operation for the most part was clean. There was a lot there to like. Certainly a lot to clean up … but a lot to build on."The performance adds to Sanders' experience after a challenging first season. In 2025, he appeared in eight games and made seven starts, finishing with a 3-4 record as a starter. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions while completing 56.6% of his passes.In 2026, Sanders has completed 22 of 34 attempts for 299 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions across three appearances.There were also questions about his future after Sanders hired a new agent, Adie Von Gontard, with some speculating that Cleveland could consider a trade. However, Cabot also dismissed suggestions that Gabriel had moved ahead of Sanders in the quarterback pecking order.Speaking on 92.3 The Fan's Cleveland radio show with Ken Carman and Tony Grossi, Cabot made her position clear."Shedeur Sanders, and I wrote this last week, is still the No. 2 quarterback, and he is still the next man up, and if, for some reason, Deshaun Watson can't fulfill his duties, Shedeur Sanders will play."With Cleveland reportedly ruling out Jones, Sanders retains his place behind Watson. His Saints performance has given him something to build on, but the next challenge is turning that opportunity into consistent production whenever the Browns call his number.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The Washington Commanders offense was stuck in neutral throughout the first half of Monday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and Stefon Diggs wasn't happy about it.

While the driving rain didn't help the passing attack, the wide receiver appeared quite frustrated on the sidelines and made his feelings clear:

Washington punted on its first four possessions, which only added to Diggs' frustration.

To be fair, Cincinnati's typically explosive offense didn't fare much better in the early going with two punts and a turnover on downs in its first three possessions even with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins leading the way.

But Burrow did find his footing in the rain and connected with Higgins for the game's opening touchdown.

As for Diggs, he leads Washington in catches, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns on the season, and surely always wants to be involved. And he's not afraid to let his teammates know about it.

articles.title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injures ankle vs Commanders Monday night
articles.summary: Bengals safety Bryan Cook hurt his ankle during the team's NFL Week 11 game against Washington on Monday night.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium.

Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power.

The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable.

"It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)."

Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter.

Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury.

See photos from Bengals vs. Commanders on Monday Night Football

Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter.

Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million.

"My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life."

Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament.

Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022.

articles.title: Former Patriots QB reveals sweet way daughter helps ease nerves
articles.summary: Former Patriots quarterback Joe Milton has one name he continuously repeats before big throws.
articles.body:
Joe Milton revealed the heartfelt way his daughter helps calm him down during crucial moments in a game.

The former New England Patriots quarterback, who is currently starting for the Philadelphia Eagles, is known for his impressive strength and ability to throw a deep ball. But to help calm his nerves before making a big pass and ensure it's accurate and catchable for the receiver, he says just one name: Maleia.

That's the name of Milton's one-year-old daughter.

"So, I can relax a little bit," Milton explained. "Knowing that, basically it kind of tells me in my mind that I'm throwing the ball to her, so it can't be as hard. Show a little love."

Milton helped lead the Eagles to their first victory since September, defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday and moving them to a 3-7 record.

He began his career with the Patriots , being selected in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. However, after just one year in New England, he was traded to the Dallas Cowboys, where he spent the 2025 season and part of 2026, going between the active roster and the practice squad. Then, the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys practice squad to take over for starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is sidelined for the year with blood clots.
